sections.heading: How IB Gram turns a search for the best IB home tuition in Mumbai into a shortlist
paragraphs: A request usually arrives as one sentence: a Diploma Programme (DP) 1 student in Khar West is sinking in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level (HL), and the family wants someone at the flat on weekday evenings. That sentence is not yet a brief. Before any tutor is contacted it has to become three answers: which paper or component is actually failing, which evenings are genuinely free for a whole term rather than for a fortnight, and how far the family is willing to let the search travel. Families who answer the third question honestly get a shortlist worth reading.

The sequence is deliberately short, and it is worth knowing before you write in. 1. You send the board, the year, the subject and level, your pincode and two or three slots that are real. 2. We read that brief against tutor profiles and filter on component experience rather than on a broad subject label, so an Internal Assessment (IA) problem goes to someone who has marked IAs. 3. You get a shortlist, usually a small one, with the travel time and the free slot written next to each name. 4. You take a first session with one of them and decide afterwards, not before.

The shortlist is where the discomfort begins. The tutor who fits the brief closest is often the one with the least convenient availability, because a strong IB home tutor in Mumbai fills the weekday five-to-eight window first and keeps whatever is left: a seven-thirty Saturday morning, a nine o'clock Tuesday after a Bandra session, a Sunday before lunch. A parent who treats that slot as a dealbreaker ends up with the third name on the list instead of the first. That is a legitimate decision. It should be made knowingly rather than by default, which is what happens when the awkward option is never put in front of you.

Nobody here decides which trade-off your family should accept. The job is to put the trade-offs in writing: who is free when, who travels how far, who has taught the exact component you are worried about, and who has only taught the subject around it.
bullets: 1. Send board, year, subject, level, pincode and two genuinely free slots
2. Profiles filtered on component experience, not broad subject labels
3. Shortlist returned with travel time and free slot beside each name
4. One first session, then you decide whether this arrangement continues
Awkward slots are shown as slots, not quietly dropped from the list

sections.heading: Primary Years, Middle Years, IGCSE and the Diploma: where the easy choice costs you later
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs as the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP), and most international schools here bolt an IGCSE year or two between MYP and DP. Each stage has a comfortable option and a price for taking it. In PYP and early MYP there is no external exam, reporting is against criteria rather than percentages, and a child can coast for three years while looking fine on paper. The platform's briefs span all IB and IGCSE subjects across IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 home tuition in Mumbai is requested for, and the Year 7 to Year 9 requests are almost always the ones a parent wishes they had sent two years earlier.

MYP 5 is where the slack runs out: the personal project and eAssessment are the first pieces of work a student cannot talk their way through. At IGCSE the first real fork appears. Cambridge International Education offers Core and Extended papers in several subjects, and Core entry limits the grades available while Extended carries the full range on harder papers. Core is the comfortable choice, and in a Year 10 conversation it often sounds like kindness. For a student who wants Chemistry at Higher Level in DP, it is a door quietly closing. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs a single tier in most subjects, which removes the decision and raises the floor.

The Diploma asks for six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the service requirement. The uncomfortable conversation in DP is the fourth HL. A student carrying four Higher Levels because it looked impressive in April of MYP 5 is the single most common reason a family writes to us in February of DP1. Moving one subject from Higher Level to Standard Level (SL) in DP1 is a timetable adjustment; the same move in DP2 is a salvage operation, and some schools will not allow it at all.

A tutor who agrees with every choice already on your child's subject sheet is not reading the syllabus. The first useful thing an IB private tutor in Mumbai can do, in Year 9, Year 10 or DP1, is tell you which combination on that sheet is arithmetically unsurvivable with the hours your child actually has.
bullets: PYP and MYP report against criteria, so coasting looks fine for years
MYP 5 personal project and eAssessment are the first external pressure
Cambridge Core entry limits grades; Extended carries the full range
Edexcel International GCSE removes the tier decision in most subjects
A fourth Higher Level is the commonest February regret in DP1

sections.heading: Which subject decisions will a good tutor argue with you about?
paragraphs: Three of them. Whether your child should be sitting a given Higher Level subject at all; whether the Internal Assessment topic they have chosen can actually score against the published criteria; and whether the subject they are weakest in is weak because of content or because of exam technique. Those three arguments, had early, are the whole value of subject depth. Everything else is revision.

Take the IA argument first, because it costs families the most. A DP2 student in Chembur chose perfume chemistry for her Chemistry IA because she loves it. The topic is genuinely interesting and produces no measurable range worth plotting, which means the Analysis criterion has almost nothing to reward. Heard in week two, that is a redirect. Heard in week nine, with the data collected and the draft half written, it is a lost grade band. The same happens in Physics, where a topic with no clean independent variable cannot carry an uncertainty discussion, and in Business Management, where a research project built on a company that publishes nothing usable leaves the student writing opinion.

Subject depth also means knowing which paper is doing the damage. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level carries Paper 3, a long investigative paper that rewards a completely different habit from Papers 1 and 2, and a student can be competent at both and still lose the grade there. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level does not have it, which is why the AA HL to AI SL question is a technique question and not a pride question. At IGCSE, Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 pays method marks that students throw away by answering too fast, and 0625 Physics Paper 6 tests practical skills in writing, without a laboratory in sight, which no amount of classroom time fixes if nobody has taught the paper's conventions.

In languages and humanities the component split matters as much. English A Language and Literature splits the HL essay from the individual oral, and a student strong in written analysis can be unprepared for a global issue discussion. Economics asks for commentaries pinned to real articles, which means the skill being graded is selection, not writing. All IB and IGCSE subjects a home tutor in Mumbai covers break down this way once you ask the right question, which is never 'is she bad at Chemistry' but 'which component is she losing marks in'.
bullets: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL carries Paper 3; Applications SL does not
Cambridge 0625 Paper 6 tests practical skill in writing, not in a laboratory
An IA topic with no measurable range cannot score on Analysis
English HL essay and the individual oral are separate skills, taught separately
0580 Extended Paper 4 pays method marks that fast answers throw away

sections.heading: Which Mumbai zone can actually give you the right tutor on the right evening?
paragraphs: Your zone decides your availability more than your budget does. Mumbai, Maharashtra splits into six practical tutoring zones, and each one has a different supply of IB specialists: South Mumbai, the Western Suburbs, the Central Suburbs, the Eastern Suburbs, Navi Mumbai and Thane. The right subject specialist is frequently one zone away rather than two streets away, and that is the first inconvenience most families are asked to accept. Geography is why the best IB home tuition in Mumbai so often sits one zone away from the family who needs it.

South Mumbai is short-distance and slow. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba or Cuffe Parade covers a few kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening, so matches are made inside the island rather than pulled down from the suburbs. Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Fort families usually get a tutor who already teaches two other students within a ten-minute radius, and the Coastal Road plus Metro Line 3 from Cuffe Parade towards BKC have made the Churchgate to Grant Road stretch of the Western Line less decisive than it was. The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway: Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz and Juhu in the south, Andheri, Goregaon East and Oshiwara in the middle, Malad, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar East above. Matching along that line works; matching across it, with the Bandra-Worli Sea Link or Link Road in the way at six in the evening, does not. Metro Line 1 from Versova through Andheri to Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 from Dahisar down to Gundavali have made a few cross-matches viable that were impossible before.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai is the odd one out: physically central, with no station of its own, reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, which is why a Powai family hears a different answer about a six o'clock slot than a Kurla or Mulund family does. The Santacruz-Chembur Link Road makes a Chembur to BKC run shorter than the map suggests. The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway puts Wadala and Chembur closer to South Mumbai than any resident expects.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Trans-Harbour Line, Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 from Belapur to Pendhar and now the Atal Setu connecting them outward. Tutors are matched node to node; pulling one across the creek from the island city for a weekday evening lesson almost never survives a full term. Thane spreads from the station east along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: a tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and nearly an hour at eight. A family in Kharghar who waited six weeks for the one Chemistry Higher Level specialist genuinely covering the Navi Mumbai nodes had a better year than the family down the road who took whoever was free on Monday.
bullets: South Mumbai matches inside the island; Peddar Road signals set evening timing
Western Suburbs match along the Western Line, rarely across it
Powai has no station, so tutors arrive by road via JVLR
Navi Mumbai matches node to node along Palm Beach Road
Ghodbunder Road turns a twenty-minute Thane run into nearly an hour
The Eastern Freeway makes Chembur and Wadala closer to Colaba than expected

sections.heading: When does the Mumbai school calendar make a comfortable arrangement fall apart?
paragraphs: Late September and the whole of February. Those are the weeks when Internal Assessment drafts, mock exams, the Extended Essay deadline and the Theory of Knowledge essay land on top of each other, and a tutoring arrangement built around one convenient weekly slot has no slack left in it. A family that has been coasting on a pleasant Saturday session discovers in February that the pleasant Saturday session was never going to be enough.

The international school year here starts in high summer and front-loads its decisions. Between August and October, DP1 subject changes close at most schools and IA proposals are approved, which is why the HL to SL conversation has to happen before the Diwali break and not after it. November brings Year 10 and Year 11 mocks. January and February are the crush: DP2 mocks, the Extended Essay final submission, the TOK essay and several IA deadlines, plus the Edexcel January series for students sitting IGCSE papers early. April and May are exams and study leave, and study leave is revision time, not spare tutoring capacity. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR in Goregaon East, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School at Cuffe Parade, Bombay International School at Babulnath and Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo all work to versions of this calendar, with their own internal deadlines placed a fortnight or three ahead of the official ones.

The suburbs and the satellite cities run the same pressure points on slightly different dates. Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, JBCN International School in Parel, Singapore International School in Dahisar East, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul each set internal draft dates that a tutor needs to know about in week one, not week six. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page; these names are here because their calendars set the pressure, not because of any relationship.

The monsoon is the other calendar. June and July cost sessions to waterlogging near the Andheri Subway, Milan Subway, Hindmata and the low stretches of the Western Express Highway, and a tutor who insists on a makeup session online instead of writing off the week is being inconvenient and correct. The tutor who cheerfully cancels is easier to deal with in July and expensive in February.
bullets: August to October: DP1 subject changes close and IA proposals are approved
November: Year 10 and Year 11 mocks arrive before the winter break
January and February: DP2 mocks, TOK essay and Extended Essay collide
Monsoon weeks cost sessions near the Andheri Subway and Hindmata
Study leave is revision time, not extra tutoring capacity

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid across Mumbai: which inconvenience buys you something
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the lead service on this page and the default we recommend for a student who is behind, because of one mechanical advantage: the written work is on the table. A tutor sitting across from your child in Santacruz or Bhandup sees the blank page, the skipped working, the answer copied from the back of the book, and the point at which the pencil stops moving. The cost of that advantage is paid by you. Travel time has to be paid for in session length or in a later start, someone has to be in the flat, and a usable table away from the television has to exist. Families searching for the best IB home tuition in Mumbai sometimes want all the advantage and none of the cost, and that combination is not on offer anywhere.

Online is not the lesser option; it is a different trade. An IB online tutor in Mumbai, or outside it, widens the pool enormously, which matters when the subject is scarce: Higher Level Chemistry, Mathematics AA HL, Economics, Psychology, French B, Music. Online also makes the difficult slots possible, because a seven in the morning session before school is realistic on a laptop and absurd by car from Ghatkopar. For IA work it can be better than paper, since a shared spreadsheet with uncertainty columns and a screen-shared graph beats two people leaning over a notebook. What online cannot do reliably is force a reluctant fifteen-year-old to keep writing while someone watches.

Hybrid is where most families land after a term: the tutor comes to the flat once a fortnight for the long working session and runs the weekly shorter session online, with one shared document carrying the task list between them. All IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai can be run this way, and it is the arrangement that survives the monsoon, the Ghodbunder Road evening and the February crush without anyone pretending otherwise.

The option worth naming plainly is the comfortable one. A group batch near the station, two evenings a week, where a teacher re-explains the chapter the school already explained, feels productive every single week. The student attends, takes notes, and goes home calm. It rarely fixes a component problem, because nobody in that room is reading your child's IA draft or watching her lose method marks on Paper 4. It feels better than home tuition for months and achieves less, which is exactly what makes it so easy to choose.
bullets: Home tuition makes written work visible; a screen hides a blank page
Online widens the pool when a Higher Level subject has few local specialists
Hybrid usually means fortnightly at home, weekly online, one shared task list
Travel time is paid for in session length or in a later start
A group batch feels productive weekly and rarely fixes a component
Early morning slots are realistic online and impractical by car

sections.heading: How are tutors checked, and what should you check yourself?
paragraphs: IB Gram checks identity documents, qualifications and the boards and levels a tutor claims to teach, and a profile that does not hold up does not stay on the platform. What no verification process can tell you is whether this particular adult will say something unwelcome to your child in week three. That part you check yourself, in the first session, and it is the check that matters most.

Ask narrow questions. Not 'do you teach Chemistry' but 'how many Chemistry IAs have you taken from proposal to final draft, and what did you tell the student whose topic was not going to work'. Not 'are you good with weak students' but 'what work will you set between sessions, and what happens the week it is not done'. The answer you want is uncomfortable: a tutor who says she will not run the next session if the practice paper has not been attempted has just made your Tuesday harder and your child's July more likely to go well. A tutor who says the work is optional and we will see how it goes has told you what the next six months look like.

There is one refusal you should actively want. The IB requires the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the oral components to be the candidate's own work, and a tutor who offers to clean up the data set, rewrite the evaluation or draft the EE introduction is creating an academic honesty risk that lands on your child, not on the tutor. The right behaviour looks unhelpful from the outside: annotating a draft with questions instead of corrections, pointing at the criterion instead of supplying the sentence, and declining to touch the parts that must be the student's own. Parents occasionally read this as a tutor not doing enough. It is a tutor protecting a candidate.

Check the ordinary things too. Sit within earshot of the first session rather than in the room, and listen to tone rather than content. Ask for the session note afterwards and see whether it names a component and a next action or just says the session went well. A note that says 'reviewed Topic 4' is not a note. A note that says 'she can balance redox half-equations and cannot yet choose between them under time pressure, so three timed questions before Thursday' is.
bullets: Identity documents, qualifications and the boards and levels claimed are checked
Ask which component they have taught, not which subject they know
Ask what work is set between sessions and what happens when it is skipped
A tutor who offers to draft an IA is a candidate risk, not a shortcut
A session note should name a component and a next action

sections.heading: The best IB home tuition in Mumbai is usually the least comfortable option
paragraphs: The pattern repeats across every zone of this city: the arrangement that moves a grade is almost never the one that feels nicest in month one. A DP1 Economics student in Vikhroli had a tutor who, after three sessions, told her parents that her diagram work was reproduced from memory and would not survive the Part B questions. That stung, and the family nearly replaced him. Another family on the same floor took a tutor who sent a warm note in week twelve saying their son was making steady progress, three weeks before the mock said otherwise. Feedback that arrives in week three is cheap. The same information in week twelve is expensive and sometimes unusable.

The conversations nobody wants are the ones worth paying for. Being told in January of DP1 that your son should move Chemistry from Higher Level to Standard Level is not a tutor giving up; it is a tutor reading six subjects, an Extended Essay, a TOK essay and the hours that actually exist in a Mumbai school week against each other. Being told that the IA topic your daughter chose because she loves it will not score is the same kind of favour. Both sentences are easier to say in week two than in week nine, and the tutor willing to say them early is the one you will like least in the first month.

Then there are the refusals. A tutor who will not add four extra sessions in the fortnight before Paper 1 is usually right: compressing a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches syllabus into April moves sleep, not marks, and a tired candidate loses more in the hall than a slightly under-revised one. A tutor who sets real work between sessions and will not continue if it is not done has transferred effort onto your household on purpose. A tutor who tells you the nearest available specialist is in a different zone, and that you will either travel or wait, has given you a true answer instead of a convenient one. The six-week wait in Kharghar, the Sunday morning slot in Mulund, the drive from Dahisar East to a tutor's area in Borivali: each of these is a cost in something other than money, and each of them regularly buys a better year.

IB tuition fees in Mumbai move with board and level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs, and nothing on this page will invent a figure for any of that. The more useful account is the other one. The real currency of a good arrangement is the slot you resent, the holiday week you keep, the criticism you receive in month one, and the willingness to be told that the plan your family already agreed on is wrong. The best IB home tuition in Mumbai, on any honest definition, is paid for in both currencies at once.
bullets: Blunt feedback in week three is cheaper than a kind report in week twelve
A Higher Level to Standard Level move in January is strategy, not defeat
Refusing extra April sessions is often the correct professional answer
Fees depend on level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length
The slot you resent is frequently the one the right tutor actually has

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks you should expect a change in method, not in grades. The notebook starts showing mark-scheme steps rather than final answers. Your child brings a question to the session instead of waiting to be told what to do. The IA has a variable that can be measured and a plan for collecting enough of it. If a tutor shows you a grade jump at four weeks, be suspicious of the test rather than impressed by the tutor, because four weeks is not long enough for a syllabus to move. The best IB home tuition in Mumbai looks unremarkable at four weeks and obvious at one exam cycle.

At one term the measure is component-level. A named paper should be attempted completely instead of abandoned halfway. The long-answer section that used to be skipped should be started. The internal grade may have moved by a band, or it may not have moved at all while the underlying work has, which is a normal and frustrating stage. At one exam cycle you finally have the only honest measure there is, and by then the arrangement has either held through February or it has not.

Here are the limits stated plainly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor who understands how these papers are marked would. A tutor is one input among school teaching, sleep, attendance, subject choice and the student's own effort, and on a bad combination of those a good tutor still loses. Some students do not improve on the timeline their parents expected. A session that always feels pleasant and never produces a disagreement is a warning sign rather than a result, and so is a report that is positive every single fortnight.

If an arrangement genuinely is not working, say so early rather than at the end of term. Tell us what has not changed in the notebook and in the session notes, and a replacement is arranged from the brief we already hold, with the new tutor given the component history so your child does not spend three sessions being re-diagnosed. Changing tutors twice in a term is a real cost to a student, so the first question is always whether the problem is the tutor, the slot, or work that is not being done between sessions.
bullets: Four weeks: method visible in the notebook, not a changed grade
One term: a named paper attempted completely instead of abandoned
One exam cycle: the only measure that settles the question
A session that always feels pleasant is a warning, not a result
IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor can

sections.heading: Starting IB home tuition in Mumbai without pretending it will be easy
paragraphs: Prepare four things before you write in and the first session is worth three. The latest report card or internal grade sheet, with the actual component comments rather than the summary. The full subject list with levels marked, because the combination matters more than the weakest subject. The current IA or coursework task sheet, exactly as the school issued it, including the internal deadline. And two slots that are genuinely free for a whole term, including the February weeks, not the two slots that happen to be free this month.

Tell us the practical constraints in the same message: your pincode, the society visitor and gate-pass rules, whether a tutor can be cleared for a standing weekly entry, and which room the sessions will actually happen in. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai spends real time on building access, and a society that issues single-visit passes only will shape the arrangement more than you expect. Searches like IB tutors near me in Mumbai produce a map; what produces a working arrangement is this list.

The first session is a diagnostic, not a lecture. Expect a past-paper question or an IA draft on the table within ten minutes, and expect the session to end with a short list of what is wrong and what happens before the next one. If it ends with reassurance and no list, you have learned something useful about that tutor. Ask for the session note in writing the same evening.

Which leaves the question every family eventually has to answer: how do you tell useful discomfort from a difficult person. Useful discomfort is specific, it is about the work, it arrives with a plan, and it changes what happens on Thursday. It names a criterion, a paper, a habit. A difficult person is vague, talks about your child's character rather than her method, offers no next action, and leaves a student unwilling to ask a question in case she looks stupid. Blunt about a redox equation is worth keeping. Blunt about a fifteen-year-old is not. If after a month the notebook has changed and your child still asks questions out loud, the discomfort is doing its job.
bullets: Bring the subject list with levels and the current IA task sheet
Send two slots genuinely free for a whole term, February included
Tell us the society gate and visitor-pass rules before the first visit
Expect the first session to end with a problem list, not reassurance
Judge criticism by whether it names the work or names the child

faqs.question: What does searching for the best IB home tuition in Mumbai actually get me?
faqs.answer: A named tutor, a written brief and a first session you judge for yourself, not a promise. You tell us the board, year, subject, level, pincode and your real availability; we filter tutor profiles on component experience rather than broad subject labels and send back a short list with travel time and free slots beside each name. Checked identity documents and qualifications sit behind each profile. What the search cannot get you is a tutor who is simultaneously the strongest specialist available, the nearest to your flat and free at the hour you prefer. One of those three almost always has to give, and deciding which one is the real work.

faqs.question: Why is the tutor who fits my child only free at seven-thirty on a Sunday morning?
faqs.answer: Because strong IB subject specialists fill the weekday evening window first, and the leftover slots are early mornings, late evenings and weekends. A Higher Level Chemistry or Mathematics AA HL tutor covering Thane or the Western Suburbs will have her five-to-eight weekday slots committed by August, and what she can still offer in October is a Saturday morning or a nine o'clock Tuesday after her last Bandra session. Families who take the awkward slot get the tutor they actually wanted. Families who insist on six in the evening get the third name on the shortlist. Both are valid choices, and the second one should be made with your eyes open.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Lower Parel on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with the slot chosen around the traffic rather than against it. Lower Parel and Parel are reachable from Dadar, Wadala and Chembur through the Eastern Freeway and from Worli and Prabhadevi within minutes off-peak, so a seven-thirty start is often easier to hold than a six o'clock one. Tell us the gate and visitor-pass procedure up front: a tower that issues only single-visit passes adds ten to fifteen minutes to every session, and a standing weekly entry authorisation removes that. If your building requires pre-registration for repeat visitors, arrange it before the first session rather than at the gate.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during home tuition, and what room works?
faqs.answer: Someone adult should be in the flat, and the room should have a table, a chair the student can sit upright in, and no television. A bedroom desk works. A dining table works better, because the written work stays visible and a parent passing through hears the tone of the session without sitting in it. Sitting inside the room changes how a teenager answers questions, so stay within earshot instead. For Internal Assessment work you also want a plug point and space for a laptop beside the notebook, since most IA sessions move between a spreadsheet and handwritten calculations several times an hour.

faqs.question: Our tutor says our son should drop Physics from HL to SL. Should we listen?
faqs.answer: Listen properly, then ask for the reasoning in writing before you decide. A tutor recommending a Higher Level to Standard Level move in DP1 is reading the whole load, six subjects plus the Extended Essay and TOK, against the hours your son has, and the recommendation usually comes from watching him trade Physics time against three other subjects every week. Ask which components he is losing marks in, what the SL route removes, and what the university requirement actually is for the courses he is considering. Then ask the school, because some will not permit the change after a certain date and the window matters more than the debate.

faqs.question: The tutor refuses to help with our daughter's Chemistry IA data. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is correct, and you should want it. The IB requires the Internal Assessment to be the candidate's own work, and a tutor who cleans up a data set, rewrites an evaluation or drafts an introduction creates an academic honesty problem that lands on your daughter, not on him. What a good tutor does instead looks less helpful: annotating the draft with questions, pointing at the Analysis and Evaluation criteria, explaining why an uncertainty discussion needs a measurable range, and sending her back to do it. If a tutor offers to write any part of it, treat that as a reason to end the arrangement rather than a bonus.

faqs.question: Can we add extra sessions in April, just before the exams?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but a tutor who refuses is usually giving you the right answer. Four extra sessions squeezed into the fortnight before Paper 1 rarely add syllabus and reliably cost sleep, and a tired candidate loses more marks in the hall than a slightly under-revised one. What does work in April is narrow and timed: two or three sessions on a specific failure mode, such as method marks on 0580 Paper 4 or the structure of Part B answers, with past-paper work done alone in between. If a tutor says the schedule is already as useful as it can be, that is professional judgement rather than a lack of commitment.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels, and how long each session runs. A Higher Level Diploma subject with few specialists costs differently from a Year 8 MYP subject with many. A tutor crossing from Ghatkopar to Powai through JVLR traffic is paying for that time somewhere, usually in session length or a later start. Online removes the travel element entirely. We will not publish a price list here because any figure would be invented, and a quoted rate that ignores level, scarcity and distance is not a real quote. You will get actual numbers from the tutors on your shortlist.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Separate three possible causes before changing anything. First, check what you are measuring: at four weeks you should be looking for method in the notebook and questions being asked, not a grade jump, because a syllabus does not move in four weeks. Second, check the between-session work, because a tutor can do nothing with a student who has not attempted a single practice question since the last visit. Third, read the session notes: if they say the session went well and never name a component, the problem may be the tutor. Tell us which of the three it looks like and we will act on that, not on the month.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for IB subjects, or is home tuition better?
faqs.answer: Both work, for different students and different problems. Home tuition wins when a student needs to be watched writing, because the blank page and the skipped working are visible on the table and invisible on a screen. Online wins when the subject is scarce, when the only workable slot is before school, or when the work is IA analysis in a shared spreadsheet, which is genuinely easier screen to screen. Most families in the Western Suburbs and Navi Mumbai end up hybrid: fortnightly at home for long working sessions, weekly online for the rest, one shared task list across both.

faqs.question: Our tutor is blunt to the point of rudeness. How do we tell the difference?
faqs.answer: Ask whether the criticism names the work or names the child. Useful bluntness is specific and task-directed: this redox method is memorised rather than understood, this IA topic cannot score on Analysis, these three questions before Thursday. It arrives with a plan and it changes what happens next week. Rudeness is vague, aimed at character, and offers no next action, and you can usually spot it by its effect: a student who has stopped asking questions in case she looks stupid. If the notebook is changing and your child still speaks up in the session, keep the tutor. If neither is true, change.

faqs.question: How does a replacement tutor happen if this one is not working out?
faqs.answer: You tell us early, and the replacement is matched from the brief we already hold. We ask what has not changed in the notebook and in the session notes, because the answer sometimes points at the slot or the between-session work rather than the tutor. If it is the tutor, the next one gets the component history, the current IA stage and the school's internal deadlines, so your child is not re-diagnosed over three sessions. Changing tutors twice in a term costs a student real momentum, which is why the diagnosis comes first. Mid-February is the worst moment to be starting again from nothing.

sections.heading: How we shortlist a home tutor in Mumbai who will still be there in March
paragraphs: A shortlist built for one good session and a shortlist built for thirty of them are not the same shortlist. The intake for an IB home tutor in Mumbai therefore opens with two questions most enquiries skip: which two weekly windows are genuinely fixed in your household, and how far will the tutor you are about to like have to travel to reach them. Someone who teaches your daughter well at 4pm on a Tuesday is no use if Tuesday at 4pm is when her Creativity, Activity, Service commitment runs, and a tutor who crosses the Western Express Highway twice at 7pm will start asking to move the slot by the fifth week. Neither problem shows up at the trial. Both show up in October.

So the brief we build is longer than a subject and a level. It records the board, the programme year, the next three assessment deadlines, the student's honest appetite for work between sessions, whether an adult is usually at home during the slot, where in the flat the tutor will actually sit, and what you intend to do about the Diwali and summer breaks. That last answer changes the shortlist more than anything else on it. A tutor who travels to see family for six weeks in July is a different proposition from one who teaches through the break at a reduced frequency, and both are reasonable, but you should know which one you have before term starts rather than discovering it in a WhatsApp message on 20 June.

The sequence itself is deliberately short, because a long intake does not make an arrangement last; a precise one does. Each step below exists to remove one of the reasons slots collapse later: the wrong hour, the wrong route, unspoken expectations about work between sessions, or no agreed moment at which either side can say that something is not working.

Two shortlisted tutors will often look equally strong on paper and differ completely in durability. One lives twenty minutes away and already teaches in your cluster of societies; the other is the sharper subject specialist but travels from across the creek. We say which is which rather than letting you find out when exam season arrives. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, so there is no reason for us to push one name at you over another.

sections.heading: Does the programme year change how long an IB home tuition slot survives?
paragraphs: Yes, and the pattern is predictable. Primary Years Programme (PYP) and early Middle Years Programme (MYP) arrangements usually end from boredom. Diploma Programme (DP) arrangements usually end from overload. A Year 4 PYP slot that has run two terms without a visible goal is the one a family drops in January; a DP2 slot in February is the one the tutor drops, because eight of their students are sitting May exams and there are only so many evenings in a week.

In MYP 1 to 3 the reporting is criterion-referenced rather than a running percentage, which means a parent can go a full term without seeing a number move. The slot drifts into homework supervision, the student stops preparing for it, and by week ten nobody can say what the session is for. The fix is a goal with an end date: one criterion, one unit, one piece of written feedback from the subject teacher that you are trying to change. MYP 4 and 5 bring the personal project and, in many Mumbai schools, a switch of pathway into International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) subjects with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, where Core and Extended tier decisions become real and a tutor's job changes shape mid-year.

The Diploma Programme splits the problem in two. DP1 is about load management across six subjects, Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices that are still reversible until roughly the end of the first term, and the first taste of Internal Assessment (IA) work. DP2 is about deadlines that do not move: IA final submissions, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and exhibition, and mocks. An arrangement designed for DP1 exploration will fail in DP2 unless it is openly renegotiated in the June gap between the two years. That conversation takes fifteen minutes and saves the slot.

Years 1 to 12 all benefit from the same discipline: write down what this term's sessions are for, and review it when the term ends. Arrangements that outlast a full programme year almost always have a short written purpose that has been rewritten two or three times along the way.

sections.heading: Subject by subject: where IB and IGCSE arrangements quietly come apart
paragraphs: Families book all IB and IGCSE subjects home tuition in Mumbai across the year, and each subject goes stale in its own particular way. Nobody is a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents ask about, and a tutor who claims to be is usually the one replaced in November. Subject choice across both boards, HL and SL decisions, Core and Extended tier decisions, and the internal assessments each one carries are what you are really buying, so they are also where the maintenance work lives.

Mathematics is the clearest case. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level are different subjects wearing the same name, and a tutor hired in July for one is sometimes still teaching to the other in October because nobody said the student had switched. The exploration is due in DP2 with a modelling or proof component the student must own, and a tutor who writes it is useless. At IGCSE, the 0580 and 0607 syllabuses reward different habits, and a student moved from Core to Extended in Year 11 needs the sessions rebuilt rather than extended. Physics and Chemistry decay at the IA: the practical is done, the draft is in, and then the slot has no obvious content for three weeks and somebody cancels it.

Languages and the humanities fail differently. English Language and Literature sessions collapse when they become essay-proofreading; the arrangement survives if the tutor keeps setting unseen passages and timed paragraphs the student has not pre-planned. Economics and Business Management arrangements are almost always worth keeping right through to the final paper because the command terms stay the same while the content accumulates. Language acquisition at ab initio level is the opposite: once the student clears the oral, families often stop, and the written paper suffers in April. Knowing which pattern your subject follows tells you when to protect the slot hardest.

Ask any tutor at the start which weeks of the year their subject gets quiet, and what the sessions will cover then. A tutor who has thought about the dead fortnight after the IA draft goes in is a tutor whose arrangement tends to last; one who has not will find that the parent cancels the quiet weeks and then cannot get the slot back.

sections.heading: What a Mumbai tutor's travel load tells you about your slot
paragraphs: Across Mumbai, Maharashtra the strongest predictor of whether your weekly slot survives to March is not the tutor's subject knowledge. It is how many kilometres and how many signals sit between their home and yours at the hour you have booked. A tutor teaching four students inside one corridor protects all four. A tutor teaching one student an hour outside their corridor protects the other three and moves yours, and they will be polite about it, which is why most families do not see it coming.

In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clocks are slow: Worli to Colaba is a handful of kilometres and still costs forty minutes once the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals back up, so Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar and Tardeo families are matched inside the island rather than pulled down from the suburbs. The Coastal Road and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link have made a Bandra tutor plausible in Worli for an 8pm slot, though not for a 6pm one. The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Line and Metro Lines 2A and 7, which is why Khar West to Santacruz, or Malad to Kandivali, holds for a year while Juhu to Borivali does not. Matching along the line works; matching across it does not.

The Central Suburbs are where an apparently sensible match fails. Powai and Chandivali have no station of their own, so tutors reach Hiranandani Gardens by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar along JVLR, and a monsoon evening on JVLR is why a Powai slot slides from 6.30pm to 7.15pm and then to Saturday morning. Kurla and Mulund sit on the Central Line with the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road feeding across from the west, and Metro Line 1 from Ghatkopar to Andheri has made a few cross-city matches survivable. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Wadala are closer to the island than the map suggests, because the Eastern Freeway, the Harbour Line and the Chembur monorail all point south.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes and tutors are matched node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are short hops along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and although the Atal Setu has pulled the island city closer, a tutor crossing the creek for a single weekday evening lesson rarely lasts a full term. Thane behaves the same way along Ghodbunder Road, where a tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at 7pm, while Pokhran Road and Majiwada slots are far easier to hold. When a family asks for the best IB home tutor in Mumbai, an honest answer includes a map.

sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar decides when arrangements break
paragraphs: Arrangements do not decay at random. They decay in specific months, and those months are set by the school calendar rather than by the tutor. Mumbai IB and IGCSE schools broadly run June to April, with a short October break around Diwali, a winter break, and then a spring term that is almost entirely assessment. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School in Bandra Kurla Complex, at Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, at Oberoi International School off JVLR, at the Cathedral and John Connon School and Bombay International School in South Mumbai, at Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, or at D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, are working to slightly different internal deadlines on the same external ones.

The pressure points repeat every year. Late July and August bring the first MYP summative tasks and the first DP IA proposals, which is when a new arrangement proves itself. October is the trap: mocks or term assessments land, then the Diwali break arrives, the slot pauses for ten days, and roughly a third of paused slots never restart because neither side sent the message that would have restarted it. December brings DP1 end-of-year exams. January and February are the hardest weeks in the year for a tutor's diary, because DP2 IA final deadlines, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay stack up against mocks. March and April are revision, and the May examination series closes the year, with the IGCSE October and November series catching retakes.

Naming these schools is local context only, nothing more. IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them, and families should treat a tutor's familiarity with a particular school's internal deadlines as useful but not as an endorsement from that school. What matters practically is that you take your own school's assessment calendar, mark the four weeks where your subject's deadlines cluster, and tell the tutor in the first session which four weeks those are.

Do that and you can protect the slot in advance instead of competing for it. A family who asks in September to move their Tuesday slot to Saturday for the last fortnight of January will get it. A family who asks on 20 January will be told, truthfully, that the Saturday is gone.

sections.heading: Does home tuition, online or hybrid survive a full Mumbai year?
paragraphs: Home tuition survives best when the travel is short, online survives best when the student is self-directed, and hybrid survives best of all for anyone whose term includes January. That is the honest ranking. IB Gram leads with home tutoring because a tutor in the room sees the half-finished diagram, the phone face-down on the table and the three pages of notes copied without understanding, and because a standing weekly appointment in your flat is harder for everybody to abandon than a video call. The best IB home tutor in Mumbai for your household is frequently the one who lives nearest among the genuinely qualified shortlist, not the one with the longest subject record.

The honest cost of home tuition is fragility. One flooded road, one society gate problem, one wedding in the tutor's family, and the session is gone rather than moved. Travel also prices itself into the arrangement, and when a tutor is overbooked in February, the long-travel slot is the one that moves. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can hold the 9.15pm slot that no travelling tutor can, works through monsoon weeks without a single cancellation, and opens up subject specialists who live in Thane or Navi Mumbai when your household is in Lower Parel. The trade-off is real: younger students drift on screen, practical subjects lose the shared workbench, and a tired DP2 student can look present while doing nothing.

Hybrid is what most durable arrangements turn into by the second term, usually without anyone planning it. Two sessions a week: one at home for the teaching and the accountability, one online for the quick review of a problem set or an IA paragraph. The online session is the shock absorber. It is the one that holds when Ghodbunder Road or the Western Express Highway gives up, and the one that keeps the relationship alive through a holiday week when the family has gone to Alibaug and the tutor is in Pune.

Agree the hybrid rule before you need it. Write down that any home session the tutor cannot reach converts to an online session within the same week at the same hour. Arrangements with that one sentence in place lose very few sessions a year. Arrangements without it lose a session every time it rains hard, and a slot that has been cancelled four times is a slot a tutor has mentally given away.

sections.heading: What should you check at six weeks that you could not check before the first session?
paragraphs: Before the first session you can only verify credentials. At six weeks you can verify behaviour, and behaviour is what determines whether the arrangement lasts. IB Gram checks identity documents, the claimed qualification, which syllabus and which assessment components the tutor has actually taught, and references from previous families where they exist. What no platform can check in advance is whether a tutor marks work between sessions, whether they arrive with a plan, and whether they tell you an uncomfortable truth in week five.

So the six-week check is yours, and it is specific. Look at the student's exercise book or shared folder: is there written feedback from the tutor that is not simply a tick, and has the student acted on any of it. Ask the student, not the parent, what the last session covered and what the next one will cover. A student who cannot answer the second question is in a slot with no plan, which is the most common way a competent tutor loses a family. Check the arrival time over the last six sessions. A tutor arriving fifteen minutes late and leaving ten minutes early is not lazy; they are telling you their travel load is unsustainable, and that is a renegotiation, not a dismissal.

Verify the fee basis at the same point rather than at the start. Families who search for the best IB home tutor in Mumbai often accept whatever was quoted in June and then feel trapped in November when the subject gets harder or the frequency changes. Fees depend on the board, the level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels, the session length and the time of day, and all of those can change mid-year. Much of this applies equally to an IB private tutor Mumbai families engaged directly, without any platform in the middle.

If the six-week check fails on content rather than on logistics, say so in writing, give one concrete example, and ask for a different approach for two sessions. Tutors fix content problems surprisingly often. They almost never fix problems nobody has named.
bullets: Identity, qualification and syllabus experience are checked before matching
Written feedback between sessions is the clearest sign of a working arrangement
Ask the student what the next session covers, not what the last one did

sections.heading: Why the best IB home tutor in Mumbai is the one you still have in March
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in this city do not fail. They decay, which is harder to notice and much harder to reverse. Week four is the first point: the novelty has gone, the student has learned how to look busy, and the session settles into a comfortable rhythm of going through homework. Nothing is wrong, and nothing is improving. The second point is the first term break, when the slot pauses for Diwali and nobody sends the message that restarts it. The third is exam season, when a tutor with a full diary has to choose which slots to protect, and the fourth is the student who stops doing anything between sessions, so every session begins with forty minutes of catching up on work that should already have been done.

Understanding how a tutor chooses is the whole game. When overbooked, a tutor protects the slots with short travel, the slots that pay on time, the slots where the student has visibly improved because that family will be a reference, and the slots whose family has never rescheduled at short notice. The slot that moves is the far one, the one that has been cancelled three times, the one where the tutor sits in a loud living room with the television on, the one whose payments arrive late and after a reminder. None of that requires a difficult conversation to fix. Pay on the same day every month, keep one quiet room with a table reserved, cancel rarely and never on the day, and say something specific and appreciative once in a while, and your slot moves to the protected side of the list.

The two moments that decide a whole year are the review at six to eight weeks and the long break. At the review, ask three questions and nothing else: what is the single thing my child does worst at the moment, what are we doing about it in the next four sessions, and what should I stop doing. Then the break. A tutor who stops earning from your slot for six weeks has to fill those hours, and the hours they fill them with do not disappear in June. Paying for a reduced holiday schedule, one session a week instead of two, or a fortnightly online check-in, is not charity; it is how you hold the slot and come back without a restart. Where a family genuinely cannot continue, the alternative is to agree a specific restart date and hour in writing before the break begins.

Mid-year renegotiation is the last skill, and ending well is the one everybody skips. If your daughter drops Higher Level Chemistry to Standard Level, or picks up a retake, the arrangement has changed and pretending otherwise wastes a term: reset the goal, the frequency and the fee basis in one conversation. And when the arrangement really has run its course, end it with two weeks of notice, a reason, and payment settled. Mumbai's IB and IGCSE tutoring circles are small, tutors talk to each other, and the family that ended its last arrangement badly finds the next shortlist thinner than it should be.

sections.heading: What does slipping look like before it looks like failure?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see process, not marks. The student can say what the session is for, there is written feedback they have acted on, and one specific habit has changed: working in pen on past paper questions under time, drawing the diagram before writing the answer, planning an essay before the first paragraph. If none of that has changed in four weeks, the arrangement is already slipping, whatever the mood in the room feels like. At one term you should see marks move on school assessments in the components that were targeted, not across the whole subject. By one full exam cycle you should see a predicted grade that the subject teacher and the tutor broadly agree on.

The early signs of slipping are mundane. Sessions start five or ten minutes later each week. Homework is set but not collected. The tutor stops mentioning the next deadline. The student starts preferring the tutor's company to the tutor's teaching, which feels like success and is not. A parent who checks the three process signals monthly catches all of this in week six rather than in February, and a problem caught in week six is almost always fixable with the same tutor.

Some things no tutor and no platform can promise. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anybody who does is either guessing or selling. A good tutor changes the quality of the work a student produces and the reliability with which they produce it; the board marks the work, the school sets the internal deadlines, and a student who will not write anything between sessions will plateau no matter who is sitting across the table. We are an independent platform with no affiliation to any school or examination board, which is also why we have no way of influencing a result and no interest in pretending otherwise.

The honest version of this is simple. Arrangements that are reviewed, adjusted and occasionally ended on purpose produce better outcomes than arrangements that are left alone because nobody wants an awkward conversation. Maintenance beats hope.

sections.heading: Keeping, reviewing and ending an arrangement well in Mumbai
paragraphs: Come to the first session with four things and the arrangement starts on the right footing: the school's assessment calendar for the term, the last report or set of criterion marks, the student's own list of what they find hardest, and the two weekly windows you can genuinely hold until March. Have the study space ready, which in most Mumbai flats means one table, one lamp, a chair for the tutor and no television in earshot. Tell the society gate in advance that a tutor will arrive weekly at a fixed hour so the first session does not lose fifteen minutes to a visitor pass.

The first session itself should end with three outputs: a short written plan for the next four weeks, a clear instruction about work between sessions, and a review date six to eight weeks out that goes into your calendar immediately. If the tutor does not propose those, propose them yourself. Then diarise two more things: a conversation in the week before the Diwali break about what happens during it, and a conversation in the June gap if the student is moving from DP1 into DP2, or from MYP 5 into the Diploma Programme or IGCSE.

If a tutor is not working out, tell us with one concrete example rather than a general feeling. We keep your intake, so a replacement starts from a shortlist rather than from the beginning, and the new tutor is briefed on what was already covered so the student does not repeat six weeks of work. Replacement happens more often for travel and timing than for teaching, which is exactly why we ask about routes at the start.

And when it ends because it should end, end it properly: two weeks of notice, a plain reason, the account settled, and a short message you would be happy for the tutor to show the next family. Mumbai's IB and IGCSE tutoring world is small enough that this matters in both directions, and the families who handle endings well are the ones who get the strong tutors back when the next child reaches DP1.
bullets: Bring the assessment calendar, last report and your two fixed weekly windows
Clear the gate pass before the first session, not during it

faqs.question: Our tutor has started arriving late and leaving early. Is the arrangement over?
faqs.answer: Probably not, but it needs a conversation this week rather than next month. Chronic lateness in Mumbai is usually a travel signal: the tutor has taken on a student further along the corridor, or your slot sits in the worst half-hour of their evening. Ask directly whether a different hour or a different day would be easier, and whether one of the two weekly sessions should move online. Tutors almost always accept that offer, because it protects their income and your slot at the same time. If the lateness continues after an agreed change, treat it as the end and ask for a replacement.

faqs.question: How do I stop our weekday evening slot from being the one that moves in exam season?
faqs.answer: Make your slot cheap for the tutor to keep. Short travel, prompt payment on the same date each month, a quiet reserved table, and a family that has not cancelled at short notice all push you to the protected end of a tutor's diary in January and February. Then ask in September, not January, for whatever change you will need during the mock weeks, because a Saturday morning requested four months ahead is available and the same request made in the middle of January is not. If your travel distance is inherently long, agree in writing that peak-season sessions run online at the same hour.

faqs.question: Should we keep paying through the Diwali and summer breaks to hold a home tuition slot?
faqs.answer: Often yes, at a reduced frequency, because a tutor who loses six weeks of income from your slot fills those hours with someone else and does not get them back in June. A fortnightly online check-in or one session a week instead of two usually holds the arrangement at a fraction of the normal commitment. If you genuinely cannot continue through the break, the alternative is to fix a specific restart date and hour in writing before the break starts. Slots that pause with a vague plan to resume are the single most common way good home tuition arrangements end in Mumbai.

faqs.question: Our tutor travels from Thane to our building in Powai. How long will that realistically hold?
faqs.answer: It can hold for a year if the hour is right, and it will collapse by October if it is not. Thane to Powai means Ghodbunder Road or the Eastern Express Highway and then JVLR, which is twenty-five minutes off-peak and over an hour at 7pm in the monsoon. A 4.30pm Saturday slot is sustainable; a 6.30pm Wednesday slot is the one the tutor starts asking to move by the fifth week. Ask how many other students the tutor teaches within two kilometres of your society. If the answer is none, expect to be the slot that moves.

faqs.question: What should I say in the six-to-eight week review if things are fine but not impressive?
faqs.answer: Say exactly that, and then ask three narrow questions: what is the single weakest thing my child does right now, what are the next four sessions doing about it, and what should I stop doing at home. Avoid asking whether the tutor is happy, because they will say yes. Bring one piece of marked work and one school assessment to the conversation so the discussion stays on evidence. Most arrangements that feel merely fine at week six are suffering from a missing goal rather than a weak tutor, and naming one target usually fixes it within a fortnight.

faqs.question: My child has stopped doing the work between sessions. Whose problem is that?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement's problem, and it is the fastest route to a dead slot. Once every session starts with forty minutes of catching up, the tutor is being paid to supervise homework and both sides know it. The fix has three parts: the tutor sets one specific task with a deadline rather than general revision, somebody at home checks that it exists before the session rather than during it, and the first ten minutes of each session are spent on that task being marked out loud. If the student still refuses, reduce frequency instead of ending the arrangement and revisit it in a month.

faqs.question: She dropped Higher Level Chemistry to Standard Level mid-year. Do we need a different tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually not a different tutor, but definitely a different arrangement. A level change alters the assessment load, the Internal Assessment expectations and the pace, so the plan written in July no longer applies. Reset three things in one conversation: the goal for the rest of the term, the frequency, and the fee basis, since level and session length both affect it. The same applies if she picks up a retake or swaps a subject entirely. Arrangements that are not renegotiated after a change like this usually run on for a term of vaguely useful sessions and then quietly stop.

faqs.question: How do we end an arrangement without damaging the reference for next time?
faqs.answer: Give two weeks of notice, a plain reason, and settle the account in full before the last session. Say the reason in one sentence without a list of grievances, thank them for something specific, and offer a short written note they can show another family if you can honestly write one. Mumbai IB and IGCSE tutoring circles are small; tutors in the same corridor know each other and compare notes about families as much as families compare notes about tutors. The practical consequence of ending badly is a thinner shortlist the next time you need a tutor, often for a younger sibling.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on when a slot changes mid-year?
faqs.answer: The same factors as at the start, which is why a mid-year change usually means a fee conversation. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board, the level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels, the session length and the hour of day. A move from Standard to Higher Level, an added session, a shift to a peak evening slot or a change of address all touch at least one of those. IB Gram does not publish a price list because a single figure would be wrong for most households, but the basis is explained in writing before the first session and again at any renegotiation.

faqs.question: Can moving online save a tutor we would otherwise lose to a move to Navi Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better uses of online teaching. A tutor relocating from Chembur to Nerul or Kharghar cannot hold a weekday evening home slot across the creek, even with the Atal Setu, but the same tutor can hold a 9pm online session with no loss of continuity. The realistic compromise is a monthly home session on a Saturday plus weekly online sessions. Younger students and practical science subjects lose more on screen than a DP2 Economics or Mathematics student does, so judge it by the subject and the age rather than by preference.

sections.heading: How IB Gram Matches One Tutor to a Group of Two or Three in Mumbai
paragraphs: Most shared arrangements reach us half-formed. Two mothers from the same school have agreed in a message group that their daughters will do Diploma Programme (DP) 1 Economics together, and the enquiry arrives from one of them. The first thing we do is put the same questions to the other parent separately, because the two answers are rarely identical. One wants twice a week until the mock; the other wants a fortnightly check. One expects the tutor to set homework and chase it; the other does not want homework set at all. Finding that gap in week zero costs nothing. Finding it in November costs a term.

Then comes the hard filter. Same subject, same board, same level, same year group. A group of two or three in the best IB and IGCSE coaching in Mumbai sense works only when the children are sitting the same paper on the same date. An International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) Year 10 student and a Year 11 student in one Chemistry session means the tutor teaches one child and supervises the other. Pace matters as much as level and is harder to raise politely, so we ask it on the parents' behalf, in terms of recent marks and how long each child takes to finish a past paper unaided.

Hosting and geography come next, then the rate. Shared sessions cost each family less than one-to-one and more than a third each, because the tutor is preparing differentiated work and marking two or three scripts rather than one. We put the rate, the host home, the start time and the missed-session rule in writing before the first session, and we ask the parents to agree those with each other rather than with us. The tutor is matched last, from the smaller set of people willing to run shared home tuition at all. Many excellent tutors decline a group, and that is a legitimate professional position rather than a warning sign.

sections.heading: Which Programmes and Levels Can Actually Share a Tutor?
paragraphs: Only children on the same programme, in the same subject, in the same year. That rules out most pairings parents propose. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) 4 student and an IGCSE Year 10 student are roughly the same age and are assessed on entirely different things: the first against four criteria marked internally by their own school, the second against a published Cambridge International Education mark scheme marked by a stranger. One tutor cannot serve both in ninety minutes.

Within IGCSE the trap is tier. Two Year 11 Maths students, one entered for Core and one for Extended, cannot share a session usefully, because a large part of the Extended syllabus never appears on the Core paper and the Core student spends that part of the evening watching. The same applies to a Year 10 pair where one family has settled on Extended and the other has not decided. All IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 a tutor in Mumbai teaches carry some version of this split, so establish what tier each child is entered for before anybody agrees to anything.

In the Diploma Programme the constraint is Higher Level (HL) against Standard Level (SL). Two DP1 Physics students, one HL and one SL, share much of the core and none of the Paper 3 options, so sharing works only inside a narrowly defined block: past-paper technique on common content before mocks, with the HL extension handled separately. Internal Assessment (IA) work is the clearest case against sharing at all. An IA is an individual investigation, and two students producing similar ones at the same table creates an academic honesty question their school will eventually ask.

MYP groups are the easiest to assemble and the least necessary. At that stage the difficulty is usually study method rather than content, and a pair of classmates working on method together, supervised by an IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai for an hour a week, is a reasonable thing to buy. Just do not expect it to move criterion marks the way a short, focused one-to-one block would, and do not let it become the default arrangement for the next four years.

sections.heading: Subject by Subject: Where a Pair Works and Where It Breaks
paragraphs: Sharing works best where the work is procedural and the marking is objective. IGCSE Maths is the clearest case: two students at the same tier can work the same past paper simultaneously, and the tutor spends the evening on the questions each got wrong, which are rarely the same questions. Physics and Chemistry at IGCSE behave similarly, because the marks come off in identifiable places and a tutor can point at two scripts and show two different errors in one explanation. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai might agree to share, those three account for most arrangements that last.

It breaks where the output is personal. English Literature is the hardest subject to share, because the useful work is each student's own essay, and a tutor reading two essays in a ninety-minute session leaves each child with half the evening spent listening to feedback on somebody else's paragraph. Diploma Economics and Business Management sit awkwardly in between: command terms and essay structure genuinely transfer between students, but commentaries do not. Languages almost never share well, because speaking time is the scarce resource and dividing it by three removes the reason for hiring anyone.

Subject choice across both boards is the one thing a shared session does unusually well and almost nobody thinks to buy. Two or three families with children in the same year, sitting together for a single session on Core against Extended tier, or on HL and SL combinations measured against the degrees their children are vaguely considering, get a better conversation than any one family would get alone, because the question one parent thinks to ask is the one the others had not. That is a single session rather than an arrangement, and it is worth organising on its own.

A practical rule from the subject side: share the subject where both children are broadly fine and want to be better, and keep one-to-one for the subject where one of them is genuinely struggling. The child who is behind in a shared Chemistry session learns to stay quiet rather than to ask, their silence reads as understanding, and the parent finds out in February when the mock comes back. If you cannot say honestly that both children are at a similar standard in that subject today, keep that subject in one-to-one home tuition and share something else.
bullets: IGCSE Maths, Physics and Chemistry share well at the same tier
English Literature shares badly because the output is each child's own essay

sections.heading: Where the Group Meets: Home Tuition Logistics Across Mumbai's Zones
paragraphs: The question that decides whether a group survives is whose home it meets in, and in Mumbai, Maharashtra that is a traffic question long before it is a hospitality one. Three families scattered across the Western Suburbs will not sustain a 6.30pm Tuesday past October. Three families in one tower will keep it for two years. The strongest groups we see are assembled inside a single complex or a single lane: two flats in the same Powai or Chandivali society, three households along one stretch of Pokhran Road, neighbours in Seawoods whose children already share a school van.

In South Mumbai, families in Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Napean Sea Road, Worli and Prabhadevi are two signals apart on paper and twenty minutes apart at 7pm, so groups form along the school run rather than the map. Metro Line 3 has changed this more than anything else, because the Cuffe Parade to Bandra Kurla Complex trip is now predictable, while the Coastal Road and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link mean a Worli tutor can reasonably hold a Bandra group the same evening. Parents typing IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai from this zone generally find the pool small but genuinely close.

The Western Suburbs are the easiest place to build a group. The density of international schools along the Western Express Highway means three families in Juhu, Versova, Andheri West or Oshiwara often share a year group as well as a postcode, and Metro Line 1 along with Metro Lines 2A and 7 keeps a Borivali or Kandivali tutor reachable. The Central Suburbs work inward and badly outward: Powai and Chandivali groups hold together because nobody has to cross JVLR after six, while Ghatkopar and Kanjurmarg families are better matched to each other along the Central Line.

In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Bhandup and Mulund West sit on the Central and Harbour lines with the Eastern Express Highway and the Eastern Freeway behind them, and a Chembur group can realistically keep a tutor who lives on the island because the Freeway is quick at exactly the hours that matter. Navi Mumbai groups form inside a node: Vashi with Vashi, Nerul with Seawoods, Kharghar with Kharghar, and neither Palm Beach Road nor the Atal Setu changes that for a weekday evening. In Thane, Hiranandani Estate, Majiwada, Pokhran Road and Kasarvadavali each form their own pool, because Ghodbunder Road at 7pm does not forgive optimism. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai will take a group twenty minutes away and decline the identical group forty minutes away.

sections.heading: Mumbai School Calendars and the Problem of Three Different Deadlines
paragraphs: Mumbai's international schools run June to April with the long break in May, which sounds like one calendar and is not. Three children in one shared session may attend three schools, and Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Ecole Mondiale World School, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West and Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane each set their own assessment and mock dates inside that frame. A group of three drawn from three schools therefore carries three mock weeks, and the tutor will be asked by each family to prioritise theirs.

Agree the priority rule in advance or it gets decided by whoever messages the tutor first. The version that works is simple: the group's syllabus plan does not change because one child has a mock, and the child with the mock buys a separate paid session that week if they want one. Groups that bend the shared plan towards whoever has the nearest deadline end up covering the same three topics four times and reaching March with real gaps that nobody noticed because every session felt urgent.

The pressure points themselves are consistent across the city even when the dates differ. August and September are when a group is cheapest to start and easiest to size correctly. November and December are when IGCSE mocks and DP1 internal assessment drafts land together, and they are also when shared groups most often fracture, because that is the month one family decides it wants one-to-one. January and February are the last useful window to start anything new. By March a surviving group is a revision timetable rather than a teaching arrangement, and it should be priced and scheduled as one.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page. These names are context: they tell a tutor which calendars a group is juggling and which syllabus each child is sitting. No school arranges, endorses or supervises any of these groups, and nothing written here is a comment on how any school teaches.
