sections.heading: How does a request for the best IB online tutor in Mumbai become a shortlist you can check?
paragraphs: It becomes two or three named tutors, each carrying the board, the programme year, the subject and the level they actually teach, one piece of their marking you can read, and one reference you can telephone. That is the whole of it. The phrase best IB online tutor in Mumbai describes a judgement rather than a fact, and the judgement stays with you. Our job is to hand over enough checkable material that you can make it in an evening instead of over a term.

The order of the checks matters more than most parents expect. A screening call held before the marked sample arrives usually decides the outcome on its own, because a fluent, confident half hour on video is the easiest thing in this market to produce and the hardest thing to argue with afterwards. So the written material goes first: the syllabus version the tutor works from, the year groups they have taught, the qualification they claim and the institution that awarded it, and a script with their comments on it. Read that cold. Then talk to them. Families who work in that order ask far sharper questions on the call.

Scarcity shapes the shortlist honestly, and we say so. For Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level (HL), or Physics HL, the number of people in any single Mumbai suburb who can mark to the current criteria is genuinely small, and that is the real argument for going online rather than a marketing preference. For Middle Years Programme (MYP) English or International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) Mathematics at Core tier, there is usually someone competent within a short drive, and an IB home tutor in Mumbai is then the simpler arrangement to keep running.

You are asked for four things at the start: board and year group, subject and level, two windows in the week that genuinely work around school and travel, and one recent piece of written work with the teacher's marks still on it. What the arrangement costs afterwards depends on the board, the level, how scarce that subject is, the length of the session and, for a tutor who travels, the distance. We price per tutor rather than publishing a tariff, because those five things move the figure more than anything else does.
bullets: 1. Send the board, year group, subject, level and the specific problem.
2. We check identity documents, teaching record and the syllabus version in use.
3. You get two or three profiles with qualifications stated in writing.
4. You run the sample-marking test on one of your child's scripts.
5. You watch a screen-share session before any term is paid for.

sections.heading: Which programme claims can a Mumbai parent actually check, and which are just words?
paragraphs: Claims about the Diploma Programme (DP) and about IGCSE are checkable at a distance; claims about the Primary Years Programme (PYP) mostly are not. A DP tutor can be asked which criteria a Physics Internal Assessment (IA) is marked against and what separates a mid band from a top band on one of them. An IGCSE tutor can be asked why a particular paper question carries a method mark. A PYP claim lives in how a tutor behaves with an eight-year-old over forty minutes, which no document shows you.

That split should change what you do. For PYP and lower MYP, weight the screen-share trial heavily and the paperwork lightly, and consider whether home classes are the better buy at that age. For DP and IGCSE, weight the marking sample heavily, because the gap between a teacher who knows the current subject guide and one who learned the previous version is visible in two minutes of annotation and invisible in an hour of conversation.

The level decisions are where vagueness hides. A tutor who teaches both Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) in the same subject should be able to tell you, without pausing, what the HL paper asks for that the SL paper does not, and which HL-only topics sit outside the SL syllabus. Ask the same about Core and Extended tier at IGCSE: which grades each tier can reach, which questions only appear on the Extended paper, and what a mid-year move between tiers costs in coverage. Someone who answers with generalities about rigour and depth has not taught both.

Internal assessment is the other place to probe. Every subject across both boards carries coursework of some kind, and the rules differ on how much help is allowed. A tutor who will not state plainly where they stop on an IA, an Extended Essay (EE) or a Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay is a risk you are taking on your child's behalf, not theirs. The honest answer sounds like a limit: they will question a method, mark a draft against criteria and refuse to supply a sentence.
bullets: Ask which subject guide edition and first assessment year they teach from
Ask what the HL paper demands that the SL paper does not
Ask why a Core candidate cannot reach the top IGCSE grades
Ask where exactly they stop helping on an IA or EE
For PYP, judge the trial lesson and discount the paperwork

sections.heading: The sample-marking test: one script, one band, one reason
paragraphs: This is the single most useful check available to a parent, and it costs nothing. Send one piece of your child's recent work, unmarked if you can get it that way, and ask the tutor two questions: what band would this get, and why that band rather than the one above it. A teacher who marks for a living answers in criteria and quotes the script back at you. Someone who does not will praise the effort, mention structure, and never name a descriptor. Run this across all IB and IGCSE subjects any tutor in Mumbai claims to cover and the shortlist thins out quickly.

The answers look different by subject, which is why one sample is worth more than three references. On a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches script, a real marker points at where method marks were lost and where an answer was correct but unearned. On a Physics IA, they talk about the uncertainty treatment and whether the conclusion is supported by the data rather than by the hypothesis. On an English Language and Literature guided analysis, they show you the difference between a point about a technique and a point about an effect. On Economics Paper 2, they look for the diagram doing work in the argument instead of decorating it.

Cambridge International Education papers reward the same test. On IGCSE Mathematics, ask why a question is worth four marks and where the working had to appear. On IGCSE English, ask what the reading question is actually testing, because a confident tutor will tell you it is not the same skill as the directed writing task. On Biology or Chemistry, ask what a command word like explain requires that describe does not. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits close enough that a good teacher will name the differences rather than pretend there are none.

Parents also use this test when choosing a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families ask about, because the same marked script can go to two candidates at once. Their two replies side by side tell you more than any profile, and the comparison is free. If one tutor writes a band with a reason and the other writes encouragement, you have your answer before the first session is booked.
bullets: Send one script and ask for a band plus the reason for it
A real marker quotes your child's own sentences back at you

sections.heading: Where in Mumbai does going online widen a genuinely thin pool?
paragraphs: Everywhere for scarce subjects, and almost nowhere for common ones. In South Mumbai, families in Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Peddar Road and Malabar Hill have decent local supply for Mathematics and English, served by the Western Line out of Churchgate and Grant Road, the Harbour Line from CSMT, Metro Line 3 towards Bandra Kurla Complex and now the Coastal Road. The pool goes thin at HL Chemistry and at any second language, and that is where going online stops being a convenience and becomes the only way to get the right teacher. In the Western Suburbs, Bandra West, Khar West, Juhu, Andheri West and Borivali sit along the Western Express Highway, the Western Line and Metro Lines 1, 2A and 7, so a tutor can usually reach you, though at six in the evening the Bandra Worli Sea Link decides whether they arrive on time.

The Central and Eastern Suburbs behave differently. Powai and Chandivali hang off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road with no station of their own, so tutors come by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road carries the rest. Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup, Mulund and Wadala are strung along the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway, with the Eastern Freeway making the island city far closer than the map suggests. For a DP2 student in Mulund needing HL Economics in January, searching for IB tutors near me in Mumbai returns the wrong answer: the specialist is in Andheri or in another city altogether, and a screen is the only practical way to reach them.

Across the creek the arithmetic is sharper still. Navi Mumbai is built in nodes, Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Seawoods, Kharghar and Panvel, each a short run from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and the Atal Setu now shortening the trip from the island. Pulling an island-city tutor across for a weekday evening slot rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads from the station out along Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Ghodbunder Road and Kasarvadavali, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets everyone's timetable: twenty minutes off peak, close to an hour in the evening. Both places have real local teachers for mainstream subjects and almost none for the rare ones.

So the honest rule in Mumbai, Maharashtra is this: online widens the pool, and it is worth the widening exactly when the subject is scarce, the level is high or the calendar is tight. For a Core-tier IGCSE student in Kandivali East who needs someone in the room to stop the phone being picked up, all IB and IGCSE subjects through home classes Mumbai families already run will beat any screen. The best IB online tutor in Mumbai for a Panvel family may well live in Pune or Bengaluru, and that is a feature of online, not a compromise.
bullets: South Mumbai: good generalist supply, thin at HL Chemistry and second languages
Western Suburbs: dense along the line, slow across it after six
Powai and Chandivali reached only by road from Andheri East or Ghatkopar
Navi Mumbai and Thane: strong local generalists, very few rare-subject specialists
Scarce subject, high level or tight deadline: online wins on supply

sections.heading: When does the Mumbai school calendar leave you time to check a tutor properly?
paragraphs: June to August, and almost never after October. The academic year at schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School in Bandra Kurla Complex, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Oberoi International School on the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort and NES International School in Mulund West opens while the monsoon is still running, and the first two months are the only stretch in the year when a family has the slack to send a sample script, wait for marking, telephone a reference and watch a trial session without a deadline pressing.

By late September the DP2 calendar closes in. Internal Assessment drafts in the sciences and Mathematics land within weeks of each other, the Extended Essay reaches its final deadline, and the Theory of Knowledge essay follows once the school's own prompts are issued. Diwali falls in that window and takes a fortnight out of it. A family that starts looking for a tutor in that period is choosing under pressure, which is precisely when verification gets skipped and a confident call wins the booking. IGCSE families hit the same wall slightly later, with coursework and mocks stacked against the May and June series.

There is a second honest window in the fortnight after mocks, usually in January or February. The marks are real, the gaps are specific, and a tutor can be judged on whether their reading of the mock script matches the teacher's. It is a short window and it is the last one: a tutor hired three weeks before a paper is a damage-limitation measure, not a match, and should be judged as one.

Naming these schools is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school on this page or with any examination board, and we have no visibility into a school's internal marks or predicted grades beyond what you choose to share with us. We also do not guarantee grades, from any tutor, in any setting, online or at your table.
bullets: June to August: the only unpressured window for a full verification run
Late September to November: IA drafts, EE deadline and TOK essay together
Diwali removes a fortnight from the tightest part of the DP2 year
Post-mock January or February: real marks, specific gaps, short window

sections.heading: Home tuition first, then online and hybrid: what does each setting let you verify?
paragraphs: A home tutor is the easiest person in the world to check, which is why IB home tuition in Mumbai remains the lead arrangement for most families here. You meet them. You see how they sit with your child, whether the phone goes face down, whether they bring the subject guide or expect the student to produce it. You hear the session from the next room. None of that requires a test or a reference, and for PYP, MYP and Core-tier IGCSE students it is usually worth more than a wider choice of teacher. An IB home tutor in Mumbai also absorbs the small things: a printed past paper, a diagram sketched on the back of it, a parent catching the end of the hour.

Online trades that visibility for supply, and the trade is sometimes clearly correct. It removes travel from the equation, which in this city is the main reason a weekly slot collapses by November, and it opens the whole country for HL Chemistry, Further Mathematics, Japanese or Economics at the top band. What it costs you is exactly what this page is about: every signal you would have read in a hallway now has to be replaced with a deliberate check. That is doable, but it has to be done, and the best IB online tuition in Mumbai is simply the arrangement where those checks were run properly before term started.

Hybrid is underrated and often the right answer. A fortnightly visit from an IB private tutor Mumbai parents can telephone, plus weekly online sessions with the subject specialist, gives you a human being who has physically met your child and a teacher who actually knows the paper. It also gives you two independent opinions when something is going wrong, which is far more useful than one. The cost is coordination: two people have to agree on what is being covered, and someone has to keep that written down.

Choose on three things rather than on preference. The child's age and self-management, because a fourteen-year-old alone in a room with a laptop is a different proposition from a seventeen-year-old with mock results in front of her. The scarcity of the subject, because there is no point insisting on a visit if nobody within reach can mark the paper. And the travel reality of your address, because a slot that needs forty minutes on Ghodbunder Road at seven in the evening will not last until March, whatever anyone promises in June.
bullets: Home: verification is almost free because you are in the building
Online: wider supply, but every hallway signal must be replaced deliberately
Hybrid: a local visitor plus a remote specialist, and two honest opinions
Younger or easily distracted students usually do better with someone present
Scarce subject at HL: online is often the only way to reach the right teacher

sections.heading: How do you check a teacher you will never meet?
paragraphs: With three checks, in this order: a marked sample, a screen-share trial, and a reference on the telephone. On our side we see identity documents, we confirm the qualification with the awarding institution where it can be confirmed, and we ask for the subject guide edition they teach from. What we cannot do is sit in your flat and watch your child's face at minute thirty-five, which is why the parent-side checks are not a formality. A family that runs all three and still chooses badly has at least chosen on evidence, and that is the most anyone can honestly offer about the best IB online tutor in Mumbai.

The screen-share trial shows you things a conversation cannot. Watch what happens in the first five minutes: does the tutor open your child's actual script, or their own slides? Does the student ever hold the pen, or is it a lecture with a shared screen? When your child says something wrong, does the tutor correct it and move on, or stop and find out why the mistake happened? A session where the student annotates a document while the tutor questions them is teaching. A session where a deck advances for fifty minutes is a presentation, and you will not know for two months that nothing was learned.

References need a phone number, not an email. Ask for one parent of a current or recent student and telephone them. The useful questions are specific and small: did sessions start on time, did the tutor ever cancel at short notice, what happened the week before the IA deadline, did your child's marks on school assessments move or just the mood, and would you book them again for a sibling. Vagueness on a call is informative in a way that vagueness in writing is not, and a tutor who cannot produce a single contactable parent after several years of teaching has told you something.

Qualifications are the awkward one, because you will never see the certificate. Ask in writing for the degree, the awarding university, the year, and the schools where they taught with the years attached, then verify at one remove: a university registry or an alumni verification service confirms a degree, and a school's own staff listing or a polite call to the front office confirms a posting. It is not rude if you say why. The sentence that works is simply that you check this for everyone before a term is booked, and a genuine teacher will offer the details before you finish asking.
bullets: Marked sample, screen-share trial, telephone reference, in that order
In the first five minutes, see who is holding the pen
Ask the reference about cancellations and the week before a deadline
Get the degree, university and year in writing, then verify at one remove
Say plainly that you check this for everyone; it stops being rude

sections.heading: The remote warning signs: no camera, old slides, and a term paid up front
paragraphs: Some signals only exist online, and each one has an innocent explanation that is worth exactly one hearing. A tutor who will not switch the camera on for the trial has told you the most important thing on this page, because teaching is a face-to-face act and the first session is when a student decides whether to admit confusion. Slides that clearly predate the current subject guide are the second signal: ask for the edition and the first assessment year, and if the deck still shows a retired topic or an old command-word list, the teaching is being delivered from memory of an older course. Vagueness about which syllabus they teach belongs in the same bracket, and so does a session that turns out to be a lecture.

Payment is the one that costs real money. Pressure to pay a term up front, before any marking has been seen or any trial watched, inverts the order of every check described here, and the reason it is pushed is that it works. The reasonable arrangement is a short cycle at the start, four sessions or a month, with the written basics agreed first and a longer commitment only after the first review. Anyone unwilling to teach four sessions on those terms is telling you how much confidence they have in the first four.

Time zones deserve plain speech rather than optimism. A tutor in the Gulf is an hour and a half behind Indian Standard Time and poses no real problem. One in London is four and a half or five and a half hours behind depending on the season, which turns a Mumbai seven o'clock evening slot into their early afternoon and is fine, while a Mumbai morning slot is impossible. One in Singapore or Melbourne is ahead, so your child's evening is their late night and the arrangement will quietly decay. Ask for the city, the local time of your proposed slot, and what happens when clocks change in March and October.

Then write down the basics, because they protect the tutor as much as the family. The written items are short: session length and weekly day and time, the rate and what it covers, how much notice cancels a session on either side, who is in the room with a minor and whether sessions are recorded, where the shared files live, and when the first review happens. Online makes these easier to forget and more expensive to have forgotten. What IB tuition fees in Mumbai turn out to be matters much less than whether both sides agreed, in writing, what a missed Tuesday costs.
bullets: No camera on the trial is the signal that should end the conversation
Ask for the subject guide edition and first assessment year, then check the deck
Refuse a term paid in advance; agree four sessions and a review
Get the tutor's city and the local time of your slot in writing
Agree notice periods, recording, file location and review date before session one

sections.heading: What checking cannot promise: four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: Verification buys you a competent, honest teacher. It does not buy a grade, and we do not guarantee one. At four weeks the only fair question is whether the diagnosis was right: the tutor should be able to name two or three specific weaknesses, show you where they appear in your child's work, and describe what is being done about each. Marks usually have not moved yet and should not be expected to. What should have changed is the quality of the conversation at home, from my child is bad at Physics to my child loses marks on uncertainty and on describing a method.

At one term, look for movement on school assessments rather than on the tutor's own exercises, and for one behaviour you can see: a draft started a week earlier, a question asked of the school teacher, a past paper attempted without being told. For a DP2 student that term includes the IA and Extended Essay crunch, so judge the term on how that period went, not on a single test score in a fortnight when nobody slept.

At one exam cycle the measure is the gap between predicted and final, and the honest framing is that many things sit outside a tutor's reach: the school's own teaching, illness in May, a paper that favours topics the student happened to dislike. A good tutor narrows the range of likely outcomes. Nobody controls the point inside it, and any promise otherwise should end the arrangement on the spot.

When it is not working, say so early and in writing. Tell us what you have observed, the sessions and the dates, and what you have already raised with the tutor. We take it up with them first, because a mismatch of pace or style is often fixable in one conversation, and replacing a teacher costs the student two weeks of continuity. If it is not fixable we move you, and the next tutor is briefed on what went wrong so you are not starting from the beginning. The same applies in reverse for IB home tuition in Mumbai: a tutor who cannot make a slot work is better off saying it in week two than in week ten.
bullets: Four weeks: a specific diagnosis you can see in the work, not marks
One term: movement on school assessments plus one visible change in habits
One exam cycle: a narrower range of outcomes, never a promised number
Report problems with dates and observations, not a general feeling
We raise it with the tutor first, then replace with a full briefing

sections.heading: Starting IB home tuition or online tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Have four things on the table before you write to us and the first week will do real work. One recent piece of marked written work, photographed page by page. The subject, level and board exactly as the school writes them, including HL or SL, or Core or Extended. Two time windows in the week that survive school, travel and whatever else your child does on a Thursday. And one sentence about what you actually want: a grade lifted, an IA rescued, a subject stopped from collapsing before the next tier decision.

The first session then has a job rather than a greeting. The tutor should spend most of it on your child's own work, finish by naming two or three specific gaps, and state what the next three sessions will cover. Ask for that in a message afterwards, not because tutors forget, but because a plan written down in week one is the thing you compare against in week six. If a tutor cannot produce three lines of plan after an hour with the script, that is a result too.

For families choosing online, run the checks in the order on this page and run them before the money moves: sample marking, a trial you watch, one telephone reference, the written basics. For families choosing a tutor in the room, the building logistics are worth settling in the same week, because gate passes, a standing visitor entry and a table that is not the dining table during dinner are what make a weekly slot survive to March.

A last piece of plain speech. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school, examination board or international organisation named here, and no tutor on it can guarantee a grade. What we can do is make a teacher in another city as checkable as one who rings your doorbell, and then get out of the way while you decide.
bullets: Photograph one marked script page by page before you write in
Give the board, subject and level exactly as the school writes them
Name two weekly windows that survive school, travel and tuition already booked
Ask for three lines of plan in writing after the first session
Settle gate passes and the study table in the same week

faqs.question: Can I ask a tutor to mark one of my child's scripts before I pay anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should ask every candidate on the shortlist. Send one recent piece of work, ideally without the school's marks visible, and ask two questions: what band would this get, and why that band rather than the one above. A teacher who marks regularly replies in criteria and quotes your child's own sentences. A weaker candidate praises the effort and talks about structure without naming a single descriptor. Sending the same script to two tutors and reading the replies side by side is the cheapest and most informative check available to a parent, and it takes an evening.

faqs.question: A neighbour recommended our last tutor. How do I replace that when the teacher lives in another city?
faqs.answer: You replace it with one telephone reference and one trial you watch, because the neighbour signal does not exist online and pretending otherwise is how families get caught. Ask the tutor for a parent of a current or recent student, with a phone number, and call. Then watch a screen-share session yourself rather than reading a review. Between them these two checks cover most of what a neighbour was actually telling you: that the person turns up, that they are pleasant to a teenager, and that someone trusted them for long enough to have an opinion.

faqs.question: What exactly should I ask the reference once I have them on the phone?
faqs.answer: Ask small, factual questions rather than for an overall verdict. Did sessions start on time. Did the tutor cancel at short notice, and how often. What happened in the week before an IA or coursework deadline. Did marks on school assessments move, or only the mood at home. Would you book them again for a younger sibling. Vagueness on a live call is informative in a way that a written testimonial never is, and a hesitation before the sibling question tells you more than ten minutes of praise. Keep the call short and take notes.

faqs.question: The tutor will not switch the camera on for the trial. Is that really a problem?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the one signal we would act on immediately. A first session is where a student decides whether it is safe to admit confusion, and that decision is made by reading a face. A tutor who teaches an audio-only trial has either something to hide about who is teaching or a view of teaching that will not work for a thirteen-year-old. Bandwidth is a fair explanation once, so offer a different time and ask again. If the camera stays off the second time, move on; there are other candidates and this one has answered the question.

faqs.question: How do I verify a degree or a school posting without being rude about it?
faqs.answer: Say why you are asking and the awkwardness disappears. The line that works is that you check this for everyone before booking a term. Ask in writing for the degree, the awarding university, the year, and each school with the years attached. A university registry or an alumni verification service will confirm a degree, and a school's own staff page or a polite call to the front office confirms a posting. Genuine teachers usually volunteer the details before you finish the sentence. The ones who treat the question as an insult have given you useful information at no cost.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on, since nobody will quote a figure?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will tell you which apply to your request rather than publish a tariff. The board and level, because HL and Extended tier need a narrower specialist. The scarcity of the subject, which is the biggest single factor and the reason HL Chemistry costs more than MYP English. The length and frequency of sessions. Whether the tutor travels to you, and how far, since an hour on the Western Express Highway is an hour nobody teaches in. And the time of year, because a specialist's remaining slots in January are not the same proposition as in July.

faqs.question: Does a home tutor in Mumbai still make sense when online opens up the whole country?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and we will say so when it applies. For PYP, MYP and Core-tier IGCSE students, and for any child who quietly stops working when nobody is in the room, having a teacher at the table beats a wider choice of teacher. The checks are also almost free: you see the session, you see your child's face, and you hear whether the hour was teaching or company. Going online earns its keep when the subject is scarce, the level is high, or the deadline is close enough that travel time is the thing you cannot afford.

faqs.question: We live in a society off Ghodbunder Road and evening travel is slow. Should we go online?
faqs.answer: Probably for the specialist subjects and not for the rest. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off peak and close to an hour at seven in the evening, so a weekday slot that depends on that stretch tends to collapse by November whatever was agreed in June. For mainstream subjects, match within Thane, towards Pokhran Road or Majiwada, and keep the tutor in the room. For an HL science or a second language, take the online session and spend the saved travel hour on the work instead.

faqs.question: The tutor is outside India. How do we handle time zones without a weekly argument?
faqs.answer: Fix the slot in both cities' local time, in writing, and ask what happens when clocks change. A tutor in the Gulf is ninety minutes behind Indian Standard Time and causes nobody trouble. London is four and a half or five and a half hours behind depending on the season, so your evening is their afternoon and that works, while a morning slot does not. Singapore or Melbourne is ahead, meaning your child's evening is the tutor's late night, and those arrangements decay quietly. Ask directly, and expect the answer to be specific rather than reassuring.

faqs.question: My child's tutor uses slides. How would I know if the material is out of date?
faqs.answer: Ask for the subject guide edition and the first assessment year the tutor teaches from, then look at the deck for retired topics and old command-word lists. Both boards revise syllabuses, and a teacher working from memory of the previous course will cover something that no longer appears and miss something that now does. A current teacher names the edition without hesitating and will usually mention what changed. Slides are not the problem in themselves; slides that advance for fifty minutes while your child holds nothing and writes nothing are a different problem entirely.

faqs.question: Will a home tutor come to our building for a weekday evening slot in the Western Suburbs?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the match is made along the Western Line rather than across the city. Khar West to Santacruz West or Malad to Kandivali works well; Chembur to Andheri West at six in the evening does not, whatever the map says, because the Santacruz Chembur Link Road and the Western Express Highway are the deciding factors. Settle the building side in the first week: a standing visitor entry at the gate so the tutor is not held at security every Tuesday, a named family contact, and a table away from the television. Those three things keep a slot alive to March.

faqs.question: Four weeks in, nothing has changed. What do we do now?
faqs.answer: Write to us with dates, what you have observed and what you have already said to the tutor. At four weeks marks are rarely the right measure, so the first question is whether the diagnosis was correct: can the tutor name two or three specific gaps and show them to you in the work. If they can, give it the rest of the term with a written plan. If they cannot, that is a mismatch rather than a slow start. We raise it with the tutor first, since pace and style problems often resolve in one conversation, and replace them if not, briefing the next tutor on what went wrong.

IB Gram arranges verified IB and IGCSE home tuition across Mumbai, and the first question we ask is not what marks your child gets but how they behave when the work gets hard.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram find the best IB private tutor in Mumbai for one particular child?
paragraphs: By asking about behaviour before asking about marks. A parent tells us the board, the school year, the subjects and the Mumbai locality, and then we ask three things about how the student works: what happens in the week before a test, what happens when a deadline is a fortnight away, and what the student says about the subject when nobody is marking them. Those answers decide which tutor we put forward first.

Subject competence is a filter, not a decision. Plenty of the tutors we work with can teach Diploma Programme (DP) Chemistry or IGCSE Additional Mathematics to the top of the grade band. Far fewer can do it for a student who stops talking the moment a mistake is pointed out. So once the shortlist is down to people who genuinely know the syllabus and the current assessment model, we sort them by manner: who runs a brisk session with a visible agenda, who works slowly and makes the student explain the step back, who is willing to spend a whole first hour on material from two years ago because that is where the hole is.

We also ask what has already been tried, because that usually tells us what not to repeat. A family in Chembur who has been through two tutors that both explained beautifully rarely needs a third explainer; they need someone who will sit beside the student while the work actually gets done. A family in Khar West whose son is two grades below where he thinks he is needs close to the opposite: a tutor who will put his own script next to the markscheme and let the comparison do the talking instead of arguing with him about effort.

None of this is a diagnosis and we do not offer one. We are a tutoring platform, not a clinic. We describe observable behaviour, match a teaching manner to it, and change the tutor if the first choice turns out to be wrong for this particular student.

2. Answer three behaviour questions: before a test, before a deadline, about the subject
3. We shortlist tutors who know that syllabus, then sort the shortlist by manner
4. You get profiles describing teaching manner, not only degrees and subjects taught

sections.heading: Which programme and level decisions does temperament actually change?
paragraphs: Three, mainly: Higher Level (HL) against Standard Level (SL) in the Diploma Programme, Core against Extended in IGCSE Mathematics and the sciences, and whether to keep carrying a subject the student has quietly stopped working on. Ability sets the ceiling on all three. Temperament decides whether the student survives the workload each choice brings with it.

An HL subject in the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme is not a harder version of the SL course. It is more content, an extra paper in most subjects, and usually a heavier Internal Assessment (IA). A student who needs a predictable weekly rhythm is often better off with three HLs chosen on purpose than four picked to look serious on a university application, because the fourth is the one that collapses in January. A student who switches off when work feels repetitive can be the reverse case entirely: moving them down to SL sometimes removes the only thing that was holding their attention, and the grade falls rather than rises.

In IGCSE, the Core and Extended fork in Mathematics and the split between combined and separate sciences get decided in Year 9 or early Year 10 on the strength of internal tests. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both set papers that reward fluency under time pressure, so a student who understands the method but works slowly can land in Core for a reason that has nothing to do with grasp. That is a pace problem. Pace responds to rehearsal with a tutor who times things, and it does not respond to a tutor who re-teaches the same topic more gently.

Lower down, in the Middle Years Programme (MYP) and the Primary Years Programme (PYP), the programme constrains very little and the manner of the adult in the room is close to everything. An MYP4 student who has learned that asking a question in class earns a sigh will not ask a tutor either, unless the tutor rebuilds the habit on purpose. This is where an IB home tutor in Mumbai earns the slot: the session is small enough that the student cannot hide in it.

sections.heading: Which component of each subject sorts students by working habit
paragraphs: There is no one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need, and anyone offering that is telling you something about how deep they go. What a subject specialist knows is which single component of their course sorts students by habit rather than by ability. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches it is the non-calculator paper, where a student who rushes loses marks on algebra they can do perfectly in a quiet room. In Physics it is the Internal Assessment, where a student has to commit to one research question and own it for weeks.

The IA is where manner matters most, across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers. The criteria reward a narrow question investigated properly, not an ambitious one left half finished. A student who cannot begin because no topic feels good enough needs a tutor who closes options rather than opens them: pick one of these two, we start the method section on Thursday. A student who begins five investigations and finishes none needs exactly the same instruction for a completely different reason. The wrong tutor in both cases is the one who brainstorms enthusiastically for three sessions and leaves the student with more choices than they arrived with.

Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) punish the student who writes what they believe an examiner wants to read. The TOK essay needs the student's own claim, defended, and a tutor who keeps handing back a paragraph with one question written on it will get further than one who supplies a thesis. The EE needs a supervisor-shaped habit instead: fortnightly deliverables with dates on them, because a single deadline in November is invisible to a student in August. In IGCSE the same pattern appears in smaller form. Biology Paper 6, the alternative to practical, tests whether a student reads the verb in the question as much as it tests biology, and English Language and Literature Paper 1 guided analysis rewards holding one idea across four paragraphs rather than listing six devices.

The range of all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai families book runs from PYP reading through DP HL Further Mathematics, and the component that trips a student up is rarely the one the parent expects. It is usually the piece that needs a working habit the student has never been taught: starting without certainty, finishing to a date, or reading a markscheme as instructions rather than as a verdict.

sections.heading: Home tuition across all six Mumbai zones and what the travel does to the match
paragraphs: Home tuition in Mumbai is a logistics problem before it is a teaching problem, and for some students the logistics are the teaching. A student who needs predictability does badly with a tutor who arrives twenty minutes late twice a month, however strong that tutor is on paper. IB Gram covers all six zones of Mumbai, Maharashtra, and the zone you live in changes what a realistic weekly slot looks like. The search IB tutors near me Mumbai parents run at ten at night is the right instinct for the wrong reason: proximity matters because a reliable arrival time matters, not because a nearer tutor teaches better.

South Mumbai is short-distance and slow. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba or Cuffe Parade covers a few kilometres and can still lose most of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, so island families are matched inside the island rather than pulled down from the suburbs. The Coastal Road has helped the Worli to Nariman Point run and Metro Line 3 has made the Cuffe Parade to BKC trip predictable for the first time, while the Western Line from Churchgate to Grant Road and Mumbai Central still carries most tutors who do not drive. In the Western Suburbs the geography runs along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, so Khar West to Santacruz West or Malad to Kandivali East works and Bandra to Andheri West at six in the evening does not. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made the Dahisar to Andheri leg usable, and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link mostly helps families travelling the other way.

The Central Suburbs are the Central Line from Kurla to Mulund plus the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR) in between. Powai is the exception every Mumbai coordinator learns early: central on the map, no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and one wet evening on JVLR turns a twenty-minute approach into an hour. Metro Line 1 from Ghatkopar to Andheri and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) are what make a cross-city match workable at all. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway puts Wadala and Chembur far closer to South Mumbai than the map suggests, which is occasionally how an island student gets a specialist from the east.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes and the node is the matching unit: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel sit a short drive apart on Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 from Belapur to Pendhar underneath. The Atal Setu has changed the Panvel to South Mumbai calculation, but a tutor crossing it twice on a Tuesday evening will not hold the slot for a full term and we do not pretend otherwise. Thane spreads east from the station along Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: a tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali quickly off-peak and slowly at seven in the evening, so Kasarvadavali and Hiranandani Estate families get Thane-side tutors and Mulund tutors cross over only when a subject is scarce. A parent looking for the best IB private tuition in Mumbai inside their own zone is usually making the better trade.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar and the months each kind of student comes unstuck
paragraphs: The calendar is broadly the same across the international schools here, give or take a fortnight, and it produces predictable months of trouble. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Oberoi International School off JVLR, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort and Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai are all working towards the same May examination session, so the IA load stacks up between August and November and the final drafts land in January and February. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of the schools named here; we name them because their calendars are what tutors in Mumbai schedule around.

August and September break the student who cannot start. The IA brief arrives, the topic is open, and three weeks disappear into choosing. October and November break the one who loses deadlines, because school mocks, the EE first draft and a second IA stop being a single queue and become three. January and February expose a subject that has been quietly avoided since the previous year, since the gap is now twelve months wide and a final draft is due anyway. March and April are hardest on the confident student, when a mock grade arrives and contradicts their own account of how the paper went. May adds nobody new to the list; it simply finds whoever never rehearsed under timing.

IGCSE families at B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane or D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul work to two series, October to November and May to June, which means one child can be sitting real papers while a sibling two years below is still in mocks. That matters for home tuition scheduling more than parents expect: two students in one flat on different series want different weeks protected, and a tutor who can only offer one fixed evening will suit one of them and not the other.

The Mumbai year has interruptions of its own that the IB calendar ignores. The heaviest monsoon weeks in July cost sessions across Ghodbunder Road, JVLR and the Sion-Panvel Highway. The Ganpati days in late August or September make traffic through Parel, Lalbaug and Chembur unreliable for about a week. The Diwali break is treated by families as a holiday and by the Diploma Programme as drafting time, and a student who needs structure will lose a fortnight there unless somebody has written down what gets done each day.

sections.heading: Is home tuition or online better for a student who panics before tests in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition, usually, at least for the first term. A student who goes blank before assessments needs the same room, the same hour and the same face every week, and a home slot delivers that more reliably than a screen does. Once the rehearsal habit exists, online can carry it perfectly well, and a good number of families settle on a hybrid.

The real argument for home tutoring is not comfort, it is information. In the flat the tutor sees the actual desk, the actual notes, the actual phone face-up next to the calculator, and the actual gap between the folder the student says is organised and the folder that exists. A tutor can fix a working habit they can see. The honest cost is catchment: a home tutor's reach is a zone, sometimes two, so for a scarce subject such as HL Further Mathematics, a second language or Economics Paper 3 depth, the pool near you may simply not contain the manner your child needs. We would rather say that than send a nearby tutor who teaches the subject at the wrong level.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai removes the travel constraint, which is how a Kharghar student reaches a specialist living in Bandra East without anyone crossing the creek twice a week. Screen-shared marking is genuinely better than two people leaning over one page, since the script sits large on both screens and the examiner's logic can be annotated line by line. Online quietly punishes two kinds of student though: the one who answers in single words, because none of the small signals a tutor reads in a room survive a video call, and the one who keeps other tabs open, because the session becomes one window among several.

The arrangement that works most often for a student who dreads assessments is a hybrid: one home session a week for the work that needs an adult in the room, and one shorter online session for drilling and marking. Parents comparing the best IB private tutor in Mumbai options on mode alone usually have this backwards. Mode matters much less than whether the tutor's manner survives the mode, and a brisk timed tutor is brisk on a screen while a tutor who works by reading the room loses half their tools there.

sections.heading: What we check in a tutor and what you should watch in the first three sessions
paragraphs: What we check is dull and specific: identity, the teaching history the tutor claims, which board and which syllabus version they have actually taught, and whether past families kept them beyond a term. We ask about subjects and levels separately, because somebody who taught IGCSE Physics for years has not necessarily taught DP Physics HL, and supervising an IA is not the same job as teaching a syllabus. Where a tutor says they handle TOK or the EE, we ask what they last supervised and what the student scored against which criterion.

What we cannot certify is manner. We can observe it, describe it and match on it, but a tutor who is warm with one student can be short with another, and nobody issues a certificate for that. So the verification that decides this arrangement happens in your flat, in the first three sessions, and you are the one doing it. You do not need to sit in the room; the evidence is visible from outside it.

Session one: does the tutor get the student working, or only explain? An hour of excellent explanation with the student watching is the most common way a bright student stays exactly where they were. Session two: does the tutor know what happened last week without being reminded, and does the session open with something unfinished? Session three: has any behaviour changed, even slightly, in how the work starts? Watch the ten minutes after the tutor leaves as well. A student who goes straight back to the question they were stuck on has had a useful hour.

Ask us for a change early rather than late. The commonest mistake parents make is waiting out a mismatch politely until a report card forces the issue in March. Nobody loses face; we would far rather move a tutor in week three. The best IB private tutor in Mumbai for your child may well be the second person we send rather than the first, and that is not a failure of matching, it is what matching is.

IGCSE Physics experience is not DP Physics HL experience; we ask separately

sections.heading: Six students you will recognise and the teaching manner each one needs
paragraphs: What people mean by the best IB private tutor in Mumbai is almost always one of six fits. None of the patterns below is a type, a label or a diagnosis of your child. Each is a description of behaviour, and each points at a different teaching manner, which is why a tutor who transformed your neighbour's son can be the wrong choice for your daughter.

The student who knows the material in the kitchen and loses it in the exam hall needs predictability and rehearsal, not more content. What a tutor should do: run the session to a visible agenda, put timed questions on the table from week one, mark the script in front of the student while the mistakes are still warm, and make the paper boring through repetition until the format itself stops being a surprise. What the wrong tutor does: covers another chapter because the student needs to be stronger, which adds to the pile the student is already afraid of and confirms that there is always more they have not done.

The student who leaves an exam saying it went fine and comes back with a grade nobody expected does not need motivating. They need their own script placed beside the markscheme, in silence. What a tutor should do: mark the student's real work rather than a model answer, point at the exact line where method marks stopped, and ask the student to grade the next one themselves before saying anything. What the wrong tutor does: praises the effort, re-explains a topic the student already understands, and leaves the belief that everything is basically fine completely intact.

The student who understands the work and loses the deadline needs structure far more than explanation. What a tutor should do: open with the calendar rather than the content, break an IA or an EE into dated deliverables the student writes down in their own handwriting, and close every session with one sentence about what is due before the next one. What the wrong tutor does: teaches a genuinely excellent hour on enzymes and leaves the deadline precisely where it was, so both of them feel productive and nothing is handed in.

The student who has quietly stopped opening one subject needs one early win, quickly. What a tutor should do: go back two years without announcing it, choose something the student can finish correctly inside the first session, and let one whole question come out right before anything difficult appears. What the wrong tutor does: starts at the current chapter in order to catch up, which proves to the student in twenty minutes that the subject is still impossible and that this adult is one more person who has not understood the problem.

The student who cannot begin an IA because no topic is good enough needs options closed, not opened. What a tutor should do: offer two viable research questions and a date, start the method section before the topic feels perfect, and treat the first draft openly as disposable so that writing it costs nothing. What the wrong tutor does: brainstorms, admires the ambition, and sends the student away to think about it for another week. Last, the capable student who is simply bored needs difficulty, not encouragement. A tutor should skip the explanation they have heard four times, go to the hardest past-paper question in the topic in the first ten minutes, and be willing to be beaten on something. The wrong tutor works patiently through the basics and loses them by week two.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks of IB home tuition in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Changed behaviour, not a changed grade. After four weeks you should see the student starting work earlier, asking a question inside a session, or handing something in on the day it was due. Grades move across a term and an exam cycle, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades at any point. Anyone who does is selling you something a tutor cannot deliver on their own.

Over one term the markers get more concrete. A complete IA draft in on time is worth more than a slightly better predicted grade. A mock paper where the marks lost are the hard ones at the end rather than the first three questions is real movement, even when the total barely shifts. A student who can tell you what the markscheme was rewarding has learned the thing that generalises. Across a full exam cycle the honest picture is mixed: some students move a grade or two, some hold a grade they had been losing, and a few do not move at all. We will tell you which of those we think we are looking at rather than promising the first one in advance.

The warm, patient tutor nearly every parent asks for is the right answer roughly half the time. For a student who has stopped trying, warmth is the whole treatment and nothing else works until it has done its job. For the confident student whose marks keep contradicting them, warmth is actively unhelpful: it is one more adult agreeing that everything is fine. For the student who loses deadlines, a patient tutor who lets the hour drift into an interesting tangent is pleasant company and changes nothing at all.

The demanding tutor is not the corrective either. Pressure works on a student who is coasting and has confidence to spend, and it works badly on a student who already dreads the subject, where it produces homework done for the tutor's approval and a quieter child. With a disorganised student, a demanding tutor mostly generates a larger pile of undone work. So the best IB tutor in Mumbai for a student who has given up is not the best IB tutor in Mumbai for one who is bored, and what we actually look for is a tutor whose default manner fits the student's current state and who can move off that default when the state changes. A student who was going blank in October is sometimes bored by February.

sections.heading: Describing your child honestly before the first home session in Mumbai
paragraphs: The most useful thing you can do before the first session is describe your child the way you would to a doctor rather than the way you would to a relative. Not bright but lazy, which tells us nothing we can match against. Something closer to this: she finishes Maths the night it is set, has not opened the Chemistry folder in three weeks, and changes the subject whenever the IA comes up. That is three facts, no verdict, and it points at a specific manner.

Three sentences is enough: what the student does when the work is easy, what they do when it is hard, and what has already been tried. Include the unflattering detail, because it is usually the one that decides the match. We are not assessing your parenting and we do not repeat any of it to the student. We also will not interpret it beyond choosing which tutor to send, because reading a child's character off a parent's description is not something a tutoring platform should be doing.

Then have four things ready. The school's assessment calendar for the term, so the tutor can work backwards from real dates. The last report, with the subject teacher's comments and not only the grades. The most recent marked script, meaning the paper itself with the marks on it, which tells a tutor more in five minutes than an hour of conversation. And a decision about where the sessions happen, kept the same every week, because a student who needs predictability starts losing it at the front door.

The first session should look diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend most of it watching your child work, asking them to attempt something unaided, and finding the earliest point where the method breaks rather than the topic the school is currently on. Expect a short summary afterwards of what they found and what they propose to do for the next three weeks. If instead you hear a lecture through the wall for an hour, tell us, because that is information about the fit and it arrives early enough to act on.

faqs.question: What does the best IB private tutor in Mumbai actually mean in practice?
faqs.answer: It means the tutor whose teaching manner matches how your child behaves when the work gets hard. There is no single best IB private tutor in Mumbai, because the person who rebuilds a student who has given up on Chemistry is usually the wrong choice for a bright student who is bored and needs to be out-argued. In practice the phrase describes a fit between three things: the syllabus the tutor has genuinely taught, the manner they default to under pressure, and the student sitting in front of them. Subject expertise is the filter. Manner is the decision.

faqs.question: My son knows the work at home and goes blank in tests. What should I ask for?
faqs.answer: Ask for a tutor who times things. A student who can do the algebra at the kitchen table and loses it in the hall has a rehearsal problem, not a content gap, and the session should look more like a short exam than a lesson: a past-paper section done cold against the clock, then the script marked together while the mistakes are still fresh. Say explicitly that you do not want another tutor who covers chapters, or you will get one, because covering chapters is the reasonable default. The sign it is working after a month is small: the student stops asking how long the test is.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be too gentle?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the commonest mismatch we see. Warmth is the entire treatment for a student who has stopped trying, and close to useless for a student who believes they are already doing fine. If your child leaves exams saying it went well and comes back with a grade that contradicts them, a patient tutor who praises effort and re-explains the topic will reinforce exactly the belief that is costing the marks. That student needs someone who will set their own script beside the markscheme, point at the line where the method marks stopped, and then say nothing until the student has seen it.

faqs.question: My daughter understands everything but keeps missing deadlines. Is a tutor the right fix?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only a tutor who runs the calendar rather than the content. A student who knows the material and loses the IA deadline needs each session to open with dated deliverables she writes down herself, and to close with one sentence about what is due before the next one. A tutor who teaches a brilliant hour on enzymes and leaves the deadline untouched will change nothing, however good the hour was. Tell us at the start that organisation is the problem. Otherwise the tutor will quite reasonably assume you booked them to teach.

faqs.question: How do I describe my child to you without sounding like I am complaining?
faqs.answer: Describe behaviour and leave out the verdict. Instead of bright but lazy, tell us he finishes Maths the night it is set, has not opened the Physics folder since the mocks, and changes the subject when the Extended Essay comes up. Those are three facts we can match a manner against, and none of them is a judgement on him or on you. Include the unflattering detail, because it is usually the one that decides the match. None of it goes back to the student, and we do not interpret it beyond choosing who to send.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building off Ghodbunder Road in Thane on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is a Thane tutor. A weekly evening slot in Kasarvadavali or Hiranandani Estate holds when the tutor already lives on the Thane side. The same slot filled by somebody travelling from Mulund or Powai tends to slip by the third week, because Ghodbunder Road at seven in the evening is not the road it is at three in the afternoon. We tell you where the tutor is coming from before you commit to a day. For a student who needs the hour to be predictable, a tutor who arrives on time every week beats a marginally stronger one who is often late.

faqs.question: Our society requires a gate pass for every visitor. How does that work for weekly home tuition?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor as a recurring visitor with your society office, which most Mumbai complexes allow once a name, a phone number and photo identity are on file. Do it before the second session rather than the first, once you know the arrangement is holding, and we will share the tutor's identity details for that purpose. Where the society app issues a one-time code per visit, send the code ahead of the slot. A tutor standing at a Powai or Kharghar gate for ten minutes is ten minutes off the hour and an unsettling start for a child who needs the session to be the same every week.

faqs.question: We do not have a spare room. Where should home classes happen?
faqs.answer: The dining table is fine, and often better than a bedroom. What matters is that the space is the same every week, has a hard surface big enough for a past paper and a calculator, and has no television in the line of sight. Plenty of Mumbai flats solve this by making the hour a household convention: for sixty or ninety minutes the room belongs to the session and nobody passes through. A clubhouse study room is an option in some societies, but check whether a non-resident tutor is allowed in before you rely on it. Avoid working on a bed, because posture decides how long a student will sit with a hard question.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, roughly in that order of effect. A DP Higher Level science or a less common language costs more than an MYP subject because fewer tutors in Mumbai teach it to the current syllabus. A tutor crossing a zone prices the travel in, which is one more reason to match inside your own zone. And a longer session is not simply worth more per minute, because the second half is where the student works alone with the tutor watching, which is the part that actually changes habits. We quote per tutor rather than from a list, and we do not publish a price table.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we arrange someone different, without a discussion about whose fault it was. Three sessions is the right moment: long enough for the manner to show, early enough that the student has not written the whole idea off. Say what specifically is not working in behaviour terms, for example he still does not start the homework, or she has gone quieter since the sessions began. That is what lets us change the right variable instead of guessing. faqs.question: Does online tuition work for a student who will not speak up?
faqs.answer: Less well at the start, and often well later. A student who answers in single words is far easier to read in the same room, where a tutor sees the hand hover over the page, the eyes go to the phone and the blank half-minute before a question finally gets asked. Little of that survives a video call. Start with home sessions until the student volunteers something unprompted, and after that an IB online tutor in Mumbai can carry the drilling and the script marking perfectly well, with screen-shared marking that is clearer than two people leaning over one sheet of paper.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram turn a search for the best IB tuition in Mumbai into a shortlist?
paragraphs: A request for tuition arrives as a sentence, and the sentence is almost always about an impression. 'She says she understands Chemistry and then comes home with a 4.' 'He has gone quiet about Maths.' Impressions are a fair starting point and a poor measuring stick, so the first thing we do with a Mumbai enquiry is convert it into something that can be checked in six weeks. Parents searching for the best IB tuition in Mumbai are, underneath the phrasing, asking for exactly that conversion.

Conversion means naming the behaviour that would change if the tuition were working. 'Understands Chemistry' is not checkable. 'Can set up a mole-ratio calculation without being told which quantity is limiting' is. 'Gone quiet about Maths' is not checkable. 'Attempts the first line of a Paper 1 question before asking for help' is. We write the restated version into the brief, send it back to you in plain English, and only then start matching. The tutor sees it before the first session, which means the first session already has a target.

The sequence below is deliberately short, and nothing in it depends on a sales call. You will not be asked to sit through a presentation about methodology, and no part of it requires you to decide anything before you have seen a tutor work with your child once.

After that first session the tutor writes four lines: what the student could already do, what they could not, what the next three weeks will work on, and what you should expect to see change first. That is the baseline. It takes ten minutes and it is the difference between a six-week review that produces an answer and one that produces a conversation about whether everybody feels good about things. An IB home tutor in Mumbai who will not write those four lines is telling you something useful early.

sections.heading: What counts as progress in PYP, MYP, IGCSE and DP across Mumbai schools
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) reports differently at every stage, and each reporting style hides progress for a different length of time. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP) there are no marks at all, so the only evidence is the portfolio piece, the teacher's comment and whether a seven-year-old can explain how she got her answer. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) you get criterion bands from 1 to 8 against criteria A to D. In IGCSE you get grades against a tier. In the Diploma Programme (DP) you get a single number from 1 to 7 per subject.

That DP number is the slowest signal on this page. A 1 to 7 band is wide: a student can get genuinely better at structuring a Paper 2 answer, pick up four or five raw marks, and still sit at a 4 because the boundary did not move with her. Two reporting cycles can pass before a real improvement shows up as a different digit. That is not a failure of the tuition, it is arithmetic, and it is the commonest reason a Mumbai parent concludes nothing is happening by week eight.

MYP bands hide progress differently. A flat 5 can conceal a strong criterion A and a weak criterion D, and a whole term of work on criterion D can lift the weak strand without changing the headline band at all. Ask for the criterion breakdown, not the grade. IGCSE sits in between: the Core and Extended decision changes both the ceiling and the paper, so a student moved from Extended to Core will show a mark jump that measures the move rather than the learning. Note which tier each piece was written for before you compare it to anything.

This is why the evidence that matters in the first two months is behavioural rather than numerical. The grade is the last thing to move, not the first. Everything on the list below moves earlier, and all of it is visible to a parent who is not a subject specialist. Parents comparing options for the best IB tuition in Mumbai should look at this list before they look at a CV.
bullets: PYP: can the child explain her method to you without the worksheet
MYP: ask for the A-to-D criterion breakdown, never the single headline band
IGCSE: note whether a piece was written for Core or Extended before comparing
DP: raw marks on a past paper move months before the 1 to 7 band
Any stage: the student can name what she is being marked against

sections.heading: Which subject signals move before the grade does?
paragraphs: Subject choice across both boards sets what you are measuring, so settle it first. A student taking Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level (HL) is assessed on a different thing from one taking Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level (SL), and an IGCSE candidate on Extended Mathematics sits a different paper from one on Core. Every one of those routes carries its own internal assessment: the DP Internal Assessment (IA), the MYP criterion tasks, the IGCSE coursework component where the subject has one. The evidence you collect has to belong to the route the student is actually on.

In Mathematics the earliest honest signal is whether the student writes a first line. A DP1 student in Chembur who used to read a Paper 1 question twice and then message her tutor is a different student, three weeks later, if she writes down the substitution she intends to try and then gets stuck. She is still stuck. She is stuck further along, and that is measurable without a mark scheme. In Physics HL the equivalent signal is whether she can state her IA's independent variable and why she chose that range, without reaching for the draft.

In English Language and Literature the strongest early test is self-marking. Ask the student to mark her own Paper 1 guided analysis against the criteria before the tutor does, write her band down, and then compare. A student who puts herself two bands above the teacher has not understood the criteria yet. A student who lands inside one band has internalised the standard, which is the thing that actually transfers into an exam hall where nobody is there to tell her what good looks like. Run the same test on an Economics commentary or an MYP criterion C write-up.

The fourth signal is the stuck list, and it is the one parents can keep themselves. In week one a student says she cannot do integration. In week six, if the tuition is working, she says she cannot do integration by substitution when the inner function is trigonometric. The list has barely got shorter. It has got far more specific, which means she now knows where the edge of her own understanding sits. A vague stuck list in week ten is a bad sign across all IB and IGCSE subjects a home tutor in Mumbai covers.
bullets: She attempts the first line of a question before asking for help
She can name the criterion or mark scheme strand being assessed
She self-marks a piece and lands within one band of the teacher

sections.heading: Where an IB home tutor in Mumbai travels, and what that does to your evidence
paragraphs: Travel is a measurement problem before it is a convenience problem. Six weeks of evidence needs six sessions, and the commonest reason a review produces nothing is that only four of them happened. So we match inside a corridor rather than across Mumbai, Maharashtra, and tell you the realistic travel window before you agree a slot. Parents looking for the best IB home tuition in Mumbai often start by asking for the most qualified specialist in the city; the tutor who actually turns up every week generates more evidence than the one who is late twice a month.

South Mumbai is short-distance and slow. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers a few kilometres and can still lose most of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at 7pm, so matches here stay inside the island: Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Tardeo, Fort and Parel, served by the Western Line into Churchgate and Mumbai Central, the Harbour Line down to Dockyard and Sewri, Metro Line 3 from Cuffe Parade towards BKC, and now the Coastal Road. The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, which makes Khar West to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali straightforward and Bandra to Borivali at six in the evening a bad idea.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR and no station of their own, so a Powai slot is reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar and Metro Line 1 only helps as far as the highway. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Freeway putting Wadala and Chembur closer to town than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai works node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line shortening the crossing.

Thane sets its own rules because of one road. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so a Ghodbunder Road slot is realistic at 4pm and fragile at 7.30pm; Pokhran Road and Majiwada are easier, and Mulund tutors sometimes cross the highway. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have changed the Dahisar to Andheri run enough that a Kandivali East tutor will now consider Goregaon East. Whatever you agree, write the slot down: a start time that quietly drifts is the first piece of evidence to go missing.

Matches run along one line or corridor, not across the whole city
Powai, Chandivali and Kasarvadavali are road-only; budget for the evening lag

sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar decides when evidence exists
paragraphs: Families across Mumbai sit very different calendars in the same city. Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School on JVLR, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, NES International School in Mulund West, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all set their own internal deadlines inside the same assessment year. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of them.

The practical consequence is that some months produce evidence and some do not. August and September are settling months: school assessments are light, so the only evidence available is behavioural, which is precisely why the baseline has to be written then rather than later. October brings the first interim reports and the early MYP criterion tasks. November is when DP1 IA proposals land and you can see whether a student can frame a research question without being carried. December and January carry DP2 mocks and predicted grades, the first external-feeling number most parents get.

February and March are deadline season: final IA submissions, Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) hand-ins, IGCSE coursework going into the school's internal moderation. A review run in that fortnight measures stress, not learning. April and early May are revision and then the May examination session, with IGCSE candidates in some schools also sitting an October and November series. If you are starting IB tuition in Mumbai in January, agree in advance that the six-week review will read process signals only.

None of this is a reason to wait for a better month. It is a reason to choose your comparison points deliberately: start the record in a quiet month, hold the review before a deadline month, and never judge a tutor on a piece of work produced in the week three things were due. A DP2 student in Mulund with her Physics IA, her TOK essay and a mock in the same fortnight is not giving you clean data about anybody's teaching.
