faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for IGCSE Mathematics?
faqs.answer: It can, but only if the arrangement is deliberately built around seeing working as it is written. The failure mode is a tutor who receives a finished answer and explains the correct method, which teaches the method the student already knew and misses the line where it went wrong. Ask the tutor how the student will show working mid-question: narrating each line aloud, writing into a shared surface, or photographing the rough sheet partway through. The best IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai for a quantitative subject is simply the one who insists on this. If they have no routine for it, Mathematics belongs in home tuition at your table rather than on a screen.

faqs.question: How does my child show the tutor their working during an online session?
faqs.answer: Three approaches work and the tutor should have a settled preference. The student can write directly into a shared document or surface, which the tutor sees line by line. They can narrate what they are writing as they write it, which sounds awkward for a week and then stops being awkward. Or for longer questions they can photograph the sheet at the halfway point rather than at the end. The common factor is that the tutor sees the attempt before it is finished, since that is when the useful interruption happens.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects would you not recommend teaching online?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and Additional Mathematics first, then the quantitative units of Physics and the calculation-heavy parts of Chemistry. These share one property: the mistake is several lines above the answer, and the answer alone does not reveal it. The practical paper and the alternative to practical are also weak online, though they depend mostly on repeated drilling. Everything else transfers well, and English, History, Geography and coursework of any kind are arguably better online because the document can be marked up by both people at once.

faqs.question: We live in Kharghar and the specialist we want is in Bandra West, so the evening commute is impossible. Is online the answer?
faqs.answer: For that subject, yes, and it is exactly the case online is for. No tutor is crossing from Bandra West to Kharghar for a weekday evening session and still turning up in month eight, whatever the Atal Setu has done to the drive time. Take the specialist online for that one subject and look for a local tutor in Kharghar, Panvel or Belapur for the subjects that need the page. A split arrangement across two tutors is normal in Navi Mumbai and works better than forcing either extreme.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on, and is online cheaper?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on board, tier, subject scarcity, travel distance, time of day and session length, and online is usually somewhat cheaper for the same tutor because travel time disappears from their evening. That saving is real and it is a poor reason on its own to put a quantitative subject on a screen. The better use of it is reach: online lets you pay for a scarce Extended Mathematics or Economics coursework specialist who would never have been available locally, which is worth more than the discount.

faqs.question: Can we switch from online to home tuition later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for one or two subjects rather than all of them is usually the right move. The common pattern is that a family starts everything online in June, discovers by September that Mathematics is not landing, and brings that single subject to the table while leaving English and History on screen. If the tutor lives within reach they can simply change format. If not, we match a local tutor for the affected subject and the online tutor keeps the rest, with both working from the same subject list.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark a scanned script and get it back usefully?
faqs.answer: By annotating the image itself, beside the line concerned, and returning it within a day or two. A useful marked script separates method errors from arithmetic slips, quotes the mark scheme wording where a mark was lost, and states what to do differently next time rather than only what went wrong. A long message describing the mistakes in prose is much less useful, because the student has to reconstruct which part of their own page is being discussed. Ask for a sample before you commit to a tutor.

faqs.question: What happens to online sessions during the monsoon and power cuts?
faqs.answer: This is where online is at its strongest and it is worth planning for deliberately. July and August weeks that cancel a home session outright usually leave an online one intact, which is the main reason to keep an online option alive even in a mostly in-person arrangement. For genuine outages, agree in advance that the session moves to the next available evening rather than being lost, and ask the tutor whether they can run from a phone connection at short notice. Most can, for a shorter working session.

faqs.question: Is online better for a coursework draft or an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, and many families are surprised by it. A draft is a file, and two people inside the same file with comments attached to specific sentences is a more precise way to work than reading over a shoulder. The tutor can leave comments between sessions, the student can respond to them, and each version is preserved so the progression is visible. This applies equally to IGCSE coursework components and to the Diploma Programme Internal Assessment and Extended Essay.

faqs.question: Can one tutor run home tuition for Maths and online sessions for English?
faqs.answer: Rarely the same tutor, and that is fine. Strong Mathematics specialists and strong English specialists are different people, so the realistic arrangement is a local tutor at your table for Mathematics and an online tutor for English, each on their own weekly slot. What matters is that both work from the same subject list and the same exam series date, and that neither assumes the other is covering study skills. Two specialists with clear remits beat one person stretched across both.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us what specifically failed, because with online arrangements the cause is often the mode rather than the person. A tutor whose explanations are clear but who never sees the working may be an excellent in-person match for the same subject. A tutor who returns nothing between sessions is a different problem. We revisit the mode recommendation and match a replacement from the brief you already gave, so the diagnosis is not repeated from zero. One month is the right moment to raise it.

faqs.question: Do we need separate tutors for the written subjects and the sciences?
faqs.answer: For most Year 10 and Year 11 students, yes, and the online split makes it easier rather than harder. One tutor can reasonably hold Mathematics with Physics, or Chemistry with Biology, or English Language with Literature, because the marking conventions overlap. Spanning the written subjects and the sciences credibly is much rarer. Since the written subjects are the ones that work best online, the natural arrangement is a local science and mathematics tutor plus an online tutor for English and the humanities.

sections.heading: How we shortlist an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai when you ask for the best one
paragraphs: A request for the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai usually arrives as one sentence: Year 10, Maths Extended, slipping since the October test, we are in Chembur, weekday evenings after seven. That sentence has already decided most of the shortlist. Subject and tier decide who is academically competent. The address and the hour decide who can physically be at your door every week for the next eighteen months. The clause about slipping since October decides the hardest thing of all, which is whether this student needs more content delivered or needs to stop believing they are bad at Maths. Those two problems are solved by different people, and the second one is far more common at International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) level than the first.

1. You tell us the board, the year group, the subject and tier, your area and the two evenings that genuinely work rather than the ones that work on paper. 2. We pull tutors who teach that exact specification at IGCSE Years 9-11 and who already travel inside your zone every week. 3. We look at their recent teaching at this level before we look at their highest qualification, and we ask each one how they would open a first session with a student who has already given up on the subject. 4. You receive two or three profiles with the reasoning written out, you choose, and the first session is diagnostic rather than instructional.

The reasoning is the part worth reading. We will tell you that one candidate has taught Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended for several batches and is blunt with students, and that another is gentler and better with a child who has lost confidence but has less experience with the harder Paper 4 questions. We do not tell you which of those is better, because that depends on your child and you know your child. What we will not do is hand you a league table. Nobody can honestly rank an IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents have never met against another one, and a platform that pretends otherwise is selling confidence rather than information.

If you come to us having already searched IGCSE tutors near me from a Mumbai address and found a dozen numbers, the useful difference is that we start from the student's actual position in the course rather than from who is nearest. Distance still matters enormously here, but it is the second filter, not the first. A tutor fifteen minutes away who cannot teach the Extended tier is not a convenient option. He is a wasted term.

sections.heading: What IGCSE Years 9 to 11 ask of a tutor that the Diploma Programme does not
paragraphs: IGCSE is a two-year course that most Mumbai schools stretch across three, using Year 9 as a foundation year before the examined content begins in Year 10. That shape creates a problem a tutor has to understand. A Year 9 student is thirteen or fourteen, is not yet under exam pressure, and is forming a permanent opinion about whether he is a science person or not. A Year 11 student is sixteen, is eight months from a board exam, and needs technique. The same subject knowledge serves both, but almost nothing else does.

Two boards dominate here. Cambridge International Education runs the IGCSE taken at schools such as Cathedral and John Connon School and Hiranandani Foundation School, and Pearson Edexcel runs the International GCSE taken elsewhere in the city. The syllabus content overlaps heavily. The assessment structure does not. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended tiers with different papers and different maximum grades, while Edexcel more often runs a single tier with harder questions sitting at the end of the paper. A tutor who has only ever taught one of these will give confident advice about the other and be wrong about the detail that matters, which is usually what is and is not on the paper.

At International Baccalaureate (IB) schools the picture is layered. A child may be finishing the Middle Years Programme (MYP) while a sibling sits IGCSE at a different school down the road, and both parents are told their child is preparing for the Diploma Programme (DP). The IGCSE years are where Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices are effectively made, because a student who takes Core Maths and does not meet the Extended content will find DP Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at HL close to impossible two years later. A tutor working across all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 any tutor Mumbai families engage should be able to explain that link without being asked.

This is why the Diploma Programme comparison is worth making. DP teaching rewards depth, independent reading and a tutor who can argue about an Internal Assessment (IA) research question. IGCSE teaching rewards something much less glamorous: breaking a method into steps small enough that a tired fourteen-year-old succeeds at the first one, and then the second. Those are different crafts. The tutor who is magnificent with a DP2 student writing an Extended Essay (EE) can be genuinely poor with a Year 10 who cannot be persuaded to write down his working.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects need real subject depth and which need better teaching?
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects do not need a specialist with a research background. Mathematics at Core level, Combined Science, Business Studies, Economics and English Language are all taught well by someone with a good undergraduate grasp and strong classroom instincts. The subjects where genuine depth changes the outcome are Additional Mathematics, Physics at the top of the Extended tier, organic mechanisms in Chemistry, and English Literature where a tutor is arguing about a text rather than teaching a format.

Take Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580. Paper 2 and Paper 4 at Extended cover functions, transformations, vectors, histograms with unequal class widths, and the kind of multi-step problem where a student loses four marks because she never wrote the intermediate line. A tutor with a doctorate in pure mathematics sees that question and solves it in two lines. The student needs five. The skill being tested in the tutor is not whether he can do it but whether he can refuse to do it in two lines, write all five, and insist the student writes five as well, every time, for six weeks, until it is a habit rather than an instruction.

Additional Mathematics is the honest exception. It brings in calculus, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities at a pace that leaves a weak teacher exposed inside a fortnight, and a student who is coasting through it in Year 10 will be found out in the Year 11 mock. The same applies to Physics once you reach the questions on circuits with multiple parallel branches, or to Chemistry once mechanisms stop being memorised and start needing reasoning. For these, ask for depth and pay attention to the answer. For everything else, ask about teaching.

The other half of subject work at this level is choice. Which subjects a Year 9 picks, whether the sciences are taken separately or as Combined Science, whether Core or Extended is realistic, and which coursework or practical components each option carries all feed directly into the DP HL and SL decision two years later. A good home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents consult will say plainly when a subject should be dropped, which is advice nobody enjoys giving.

sections.heading: Where in Mumbai your IGCSE home tutor should actually live
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is not one tutoring market. It is six, and the boundary between them is travel time at seven in the evening. In South Mumbai, families in Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road and Tardeo are eight or nine kilometres from each other and still forty minutes apart once the Haji Ali and Peddar Road signals load up. The Coastal Road has changed the northern approach, and Metro Line 3 now connects Cuffe Parade towards Bandra Kurla Complex, but a tutor brought down from Andheri for a seven o'clock slot in Fort will quietly start arriving at half past seven by the third week.

The Western Suburbs are the largest block of IGCSE demand in the city and the easiest to get wrong. Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri, Oshiwara, Goregaon, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar sit in a line along the Western Express Highway, Link Road and the Western Line, with Metro Line 1 crossing at Andheri and Metro Lines 2A and 7 running the Dahisar to Gundavali stretch above Link Road. Matching along that line works. Matching across it does not. A tutor in Malad will hold a standing Kandivali slot for two years and will abandon a Bandra slot by Diwali.

The Central Suburbs run from Kurla through Ghatkopar, Vikhroli and Kanjurmarg to Mulund on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road in between. Powai is the anomaly worth planning around: it has no station of its own, so every tutor arrives by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and a monsoon evening on JVLR can add half an hour in either direction. The Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi up through Bhandup to Mulund, are better connected than they look, because the Eastern Freeway puts Wadala and Chembur within reach of the island city and the Santacruz Chembur Link Road cuts west.

Across the creek, Navi Mumbai works in nodes. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive apart on Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, served by the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and the Belapur to Pendhar metro, and the Atal Setu has shortened the run to South Mumbai considerably. Even so, we match inside Navi Mumbai. Thane behaves the same way: the station, Pokhran Road, Majiwada and the long Ghodbunder Road corridor out to Kasarvadavali set the schedule, and a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at seven in the evening. Thane tutors cover Thane, and Mulund tutors sometimes cross.

sections.heading: How the Mumbai school calendar decides when a tutor earns their keep
paragraphs: The Mumbai international school year opens in June and the first real signal arrives in late August or September, when the first graded assessments come back. That is when most families start looking. By the Diwali break a Year 10 who has drifted is already two topics behind, and by the time the Year 11 mocks land in December and January there is no slack left in the calendar at all. Coursework and controlled assessment deadlines cluster in January and February, the final examined series runs in May and June, and the November series exists for retakes and for students who joined the course late.

Families at Cathedral and John Connon School, Bombay International School, Activity High School and B.D. Somani International School in South Mumbai work to one rhythm. Those at Jamnabai Narsee International School, Utpal Shanghvi Global School and Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, or Dhirubhai Ambani International School in Bandra Kurla Complex, work to a similar one with different internal deadlines. Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul each set their own mock weeks, and those weeks are what a tutor should be planning backwards from.

IB Gram is an independent platform. We are not affiliated with any school named on this page, nor with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and naming a school here only tells you where families in that area send their children and what calendar they live by. We have no access to any school's internal marks, predicted grades or teaching plans, and any tutor who claims to have inside knowledge of a particular school's papers is telling you something that is not true.

The practical consequence for timing is simple. The two months worth protecting are September and October, when a problem is still a topic rather than a pattern, and the fortnight immediately after the mock results, when a student is briefly willing to change how she works. Families who start IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai in March for a May exam are not buying teaching. They are buying triage, and we will say so before taking the booking.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for IGCSE in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default at this level and for a specific reason. A fourteen-year-old working on screen can look attentive and be nowhere, and the single hardest habit to build at IGCSE is written working. A tutor sitting beside a student can take the pen, point at the line that is missing, and refuse to move on. That is most of the job. An IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai also gets the information nobody volunteers: that the study desk faces the television, that the younger sibling's class runs in the same room, that the student does his Physics standing up at the kitchen counter because he cannot sit still.

Online is a real option rather than a consolation, and for some requests it is the better one. If you need Additional Mathematics or top-end Chemistry and the only tutors with that depth are in the island city while you are in Kharghar or Kasarvadavali, an IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai gives you the subject expertise without the travel collapse that would otherwise kill the arrangement by December. Online also survives the monsoon, which home tuition does not always do, and it makes a nine o'clock slot possible when traffic would have made it impossible.

The honest trade-off runs both ways. Online works well for a motivated Year 11 revising technique and badly for a disengaged Year 9 who needs a person in the room. It works well for subject depth and badly for handwriting discipline. Hybrid is what most of our longer arrangements settle into: home sessions through the term when habits are being built, online through exam season when both sides are short of time, and online in July and August when half of Mumbai is travelling. We will suggest the split rather than let it drift.

One warning about pricing logic. People assume the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai must be the most expensive one available in person, and then buy travel rather than teaching. If a tutor spends ninety minutes in a car to teach for sixty, you are paying for the car in every sense, and the arrangement will not survive a full academic year. Match near, or go online deliberately. The expensive mistake is the long commute nobody wants to admit is unsustainable.

sections.heading: What we check before proposing a tutor, and what you should check yourself
paragraphs: Every tutor on the platform gives us government photograph identification, their claimed qualifications with the awarding institution named, and a teaching history we can ask questions about. We confirm which board and which specification they have actually taught at IGCSE level and how recently, because a tutor who taught the syllabus five years ago is working from a version that has since changed. We also check that the subjects they list are subjects they have taught rather than subjects they studied, which is a distinction a surprising number of people blur.

What we cannot verify is the only thing that really decides this. No document shows whether a person can hold the attention of a tired fifteen-year-old for an hour on a Friday evening. No certificate shows whether he will notice, in minute twenty, that the student has stopped following and will go back three steps without making her feel stupid about it. That is why the first session is diagnostic and why we ask you to be in the flat, not in the room, while it happens. You will hear enough through a door.

There are four questions worth asking any IGCSE private tutor Mumbai sends to your home, and the answers are more informative than any CV. Ask which board and tier your child is on, and see whether the tutor already knows. Ask what is explicitly not examined on this specification, because only someone who has read it can answer. Ask how they would handle a student who has decided she is bad at the subject. And ask what they will want from you, because a tutor who wants nothing from the parent has not thought about the arrangement.

Finally, check the paperwork you control. Agree the slot, the length and the subject in writing before the first session. Keep marked scripts and the running error log in the house rather than in the tutor's notebook. If you are arranging an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai through anyone, including us, insist that the record of what has been taught belongs to your child. It costs nothing while things are going well and saves a month when they are not.

sections.heading: Why the most qualified tutor is often not the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai
paragraphs: A doctorate is close to irrelevant at IGCSE. This is an uncomfortable sentence to write on a page that parents reach by searching for the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai, because the search itself usually means show me the most qualified person you have. But the job here is teaching a fourteen-year-old who has decided she is bad at the subject, and a research degree is not training for that. It is training for the opposite: for working alone, at speed, with people who already understand. Three of those four conditions are absent in a Thursday evening session in Vikhroli.

What actually carries an IGCSE student is a short and unglamorous list. Breaking a method into steps small enough that the student succeeds at the first one, because a student who has failed six times needs a win before she needs a technique. Rebuilding confidence after a bad mock, which mostly means separating what she cannot do from what she did not revise, out loud, on paper, so the failure becomes finite. Insisting on written working every single session until it stops being a request. Holding attention for an hour at the end of a school week. And knowing the specification well enough to say with authority what will not be examined, which is the single sentence that most reliably calms a panicking Year 11.

Over-qualified tutors fail at this level in a recognisable pattern. They answer the question that was asked instead of the question behind it. They skip the intermediate line because it is obvious, and the student copies a solution she cannot reproduce. They enrich: a question on moments becomes a short talk about torque in rotating frames, which is interesting and costs eleven minutes the student did not have. They are uncomfortable with repetition, and IGCSE teaching is mostly repetition. Worst of all, their expertise makes the student's confusion feel like a personal defect rather than a normal stage, and a fourteen-year-old reads that in a face before anyone says a word.

None of this means depth is worthless. It matters enormously in a narrow band: Additional Mathematics, the hardest Extended Physics questions, Chemistry once mechanisms require reasoning, and English Literature where the tutor needs an actual argument about the text. It matters when a bright student is bored rather than lost, because boredom needs a harder question and a lost student needs an easier one, and misdiagnosing which is which wastes a term. It matters when a student is aiming at HL Sciences in the Diploma Programme and needs the IGCSE ceiling lifted early. Ask yourself which situation you are in. If the honest answer is that your child has stopped trying, the right tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai covers is the patient one, not the brilliant one, and that is not a compromise.
bullets: Small steps first: a student who has failed repeatedly needs a win before technique
Separate what she cannot do from what she did not revise after a bad mock
Written working enforced every session until it stops being a request
Knowing what is not examined calms a Year 11 faster than anything else

sections.heading: What should progress look like by the first mock?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see changed behaviour, not a changed grade. Written working appearing without being asked, a student who brings a question to the session instead of waiting to be given one, and a shorter gap between a topic being taught in school and it being understood. If none of that has happened in four weekly sessions, something is wrong with the match and it is worth saying so early rather than waiting politely until December.

At one term, expect movement inside a grade band rather than across two. A student who was sitting at the bottom of a grade usually arrives at the top of it first, and that looks like nothing on a report card while being the most important part of the journey. The visible jump tends to come in the term after. By the first full mock you should be able to see which marks were lost to not knowing and which to not writing, and a tutor who cannot break the paper down that way after a term has not been paying attention.

Across a full exam cycle the honest picture is that improvement is uneven by subject and almost never linear. Maths moves fastest because it is the most trainable. English Literature moves slowest because it depends on reading the student has or has not done over years. Sciences move in steps as each topic is repaired. We do not guarantee grades and we would not trust anyone who does, because the tutor controls perhaps one hour a week and the student controls the other hundred and sixty-seven.

What we will do is tell you when it is not working. If a student has had a term of consistent sessions and nothing has shifted, the useful conversation is not about trying harder. It is about whether the subject is right, whether the tier is right, whether the problem is actually attendance or sleep or a clash with a teacher at school, or whether this particular pairing has simply run out of road. All four happen. None of them is a failure worth hiding from the family paying for it.
bullets: Four weeks: changed habits and written working, not a changed grade
One term: movement within a grade band before movement across one
First mock: the tutor should separate marks lost to knowledge from marks lost to method

sections.heading: Starting IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai this month
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful instead of introductory. The most recent marked script, with the teacher's comments still on it, because it shows where marks are actually going. The subject option sheet or report that names the board and tier, so nobody spends twenty minutes establishing whether your child is on Core or Extended. And an honest sentence from you about what has already been tried, including anything that failed. The failures are more informative than the successes and families consistently leave them out.

The first session itself is diagnostic. The tutor works through two or three past paper questions at the level your child is actually at rather than the level the school says, watches how she sets out her working, and finds the earliest topic where the foundation gives way. That earliest point is usually two years back from the symptom. A Year 10 struggling with simultaneous equations is often a Year 8 who never got comfortable with negative numbers, and no amount of Year 10 teaching repairs that.

Afterwards you get a written note: where the gaps are, what the first six weeks will cover, what the tutor expects the student to do between sessions, and what the tutor expects from you. That note is yours. If the arrangement changes later, it travels with the student rather than leaving with the tutor. Tell us the area, the subject, the year group and the two evenings that work, and we will come back with a short list and the reasoning behind it, including the cases where we think online would serve you better than a tutor in your drawing room.
bullets: Bring the most recent marked script with the teacher's comments intact
Have the board, tier and subject options written down before the call
Say what has already been tried and failed; it shortens the diagnosis
First session finds the earliest broken topic, often two years back
Written plan after session one, kept by the family rather than the tutor

faqs.question: What does "best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai" actually mean when you shortlist someone?
faqs.answer: It means the tutor whose teaching style fits this student, on this specification, at a time they can reliably reach your home. We do not interpret it as the most qualified person available. Qualification is a filter we apply early and then stop applying, because once someone can comfortably teach Extended tier content, further academic depth adds very little at IGCSE and sometimes gets in the way. After that filter we are looking at pace, patience, how they handle a student who has stopped trying, and whether they can hold a standing weekly slot in your area for two years without the travel quietly defeating them.

faqs.question: Is a tutor with a doctorate better for IGCSE than an experienced school teacher?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and often the reverse. A school teacher has spent years watching fourteen-year-olds misunderstand the same five things in the same order, which is exactly the knowledge IGCSE teaching runs on. A doctorate certifies depth in a narrow research area and nothing about explaining to a teenager who has lost confidence. There are exceptions worth paying for: Additional Mathematics, the hardest Extended Physics questions, and a bright student who is bored rather than lost. If your child has decided she is bad at the subject, experience with that exact situation beats academic depth every time.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually come to our building in Kandivali East on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor is matched from inside the Western Suburbs rather than brought across the city. A tutor living around Malad, Borivali or Kandivali reaches a Kandivali East address along Link Road or the Western Express Highway reliably enough to hold a seven o'clock slot through the year. A tutor coming from Chembur or Fort will manage it in September and start arriving late by November. We check this before proposing anyone, because a weekly arrangement that depends on light traffic is not a weekly arrangement.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we will not quote a figure because an honest one does not exist across this city. Board and tier: Extended and Additional Mathematics cost more than Core. Subject scarcity: Economics and Business tutors are plentiful, while strong Additional Mathematics and Computer Science tutors are not. Travel distance, which is the factor most families underestimate and the one that quietly inflates rates in low-density areas. Session length and frequency, since two shorter sessions usually cost more than one long one. And whether the format is at home, online or hybrid.

faqs.question: Our society will not let an outsider in without pre-approval. How does that work?
faqs.answer: You clear the tutor once at the gate and the arrangement runs normally afterwards. We send the tutor's name, photograph identification and the fixed weekly slot before the first visit so you can register a standing entry with your society office rather than approving a visitor every week. Most Mumbai complexes handle this routinely for regular service providers. If your building requires a resident to approve each entry through an app, tell us at the matching stage, because it means the session cannot start when nobody is home and that affects which evening slots are realistic.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 10 and has decided he is bad at Chemistry. Can a tutor fix that?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but the first month will not look like Chemistry teaching. A tutor who understands this situation starts by finding something he can already do and making him do it correctly in front of her, because a student who has failed repeatedly needs evidence more than instruction. Then she narrows the problem: it is almost never all of Chemistry, it is moles, or it is balancing equations, or it is the fact that he stopped following in September. Naming the actual gap shrinks it. Expect behaviour to change before marks do.

faqs.question: Does online really work for IGCSE, or should we insist on home classes?
faqs.answer: It works well for some students and badly for others, and age is the best predictor. A Year 11 who is motivated and revising technique does fine online. A Year 9 who is disengaged needs someone in the room who can take the pen. The other decider is subject: online buys you depth when the only strong Additional Mathematics or Physics tutor lives across the city, and that trade is usually worth making. Most of our longer arrangements across all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes Mumbai families book end up hybrid, with home sessions in term and online through exam season.

faqs.question: We are in Kharghar and most good tutors seem to live in the island city. What happens?
faqs.answer: We match inside Navi Mumbai first and go online for anything we cannot staff locally. Kharghar, Belapur, Nerul, Vashi and Panvel have a real tutor pool of their own, connected by Palm Beach Road, the Sion Panvel Highway and the Harbour Line, and node to node travel inside Navi Mumbai holds up across a full academic year. The Atal Setu has genuinely shortened the run from South Mumbai, but a tutor crossing it twice on a weekday evening is still a commitment that tends to lapse by the second term. Online is the more durable answer for scarce subjects.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the diagnosis in writing before you change anything. At four weeks you should expect changed habits rather than changed marks, so first check whether written working has improved and whether your child is bringing questions to sessions. If those have moved, the arrangement is working and the grade will follow later. If nothing has moved at all, tell us. The cause is usually one of four things: the wrong tier, a missing foundation further back than anyone realised, sessions being cancelled more often than reported, or a personality mismatch nobody wanted to mention.

faqs.question: The tutor is competent but my daughter dislikes the sessions. Do we change?
faqs.answer: Yes, and sooner than most families do. At this age dislike is not a preference, it is a predictor: a fifteen-year-old who dreads Thursday evening will stop preparing, stop asking questions and eventually stop attending, and a technically strong tutor she will not talk to produces less than an average tutor she will. Tell us what specifically is not working, because the detail changes the replacement. Too fast, too formal, talks over her, makes her feel slow, all point at different second choices. We arrange the change without making it awkward for either side.

faqs.question: Should we take Core or Extended, and can the tutor advise on that?
faqs.answer: A tutor can advise, and should, but only after seeing current work rather than on the first phone call. Extended keeps the full grade range available and keeps Diploma Programme Higher Level options open two years later, which is why schools push it. Core is the right choice when a student is genuinely struggling and a realistic Core grade beats a poor Extended one. The decision should be made on evidence from past paper attempts, not on ambition, and it should be made early enough that the teaching year is not wasted switching.

faqs.question: Do you publish a ranked list of tutors so we can pick the top one?
faqs.answer: No, and we will not, because such a list would be dishonest. Ranking requires a single scale, and the quality that makes a tutor right for a confident Year 11 chasing an A star is close to the opposite of what a disengaged Year 9 needs. What we give instead is two or three candidates with the reasoning written out, including what each one is weaker at. You know your child and we know the tutors, so the sensible division of labour is that we narrow and you choose. IB Gram is independent and we do not guarantee grades.

sections.heading: Shortlisting IGCSE home tutors in Mumbai when there is already a tutor to replace
paragraphs: A replacement request is a different problem from a first request, and most families brief it as though it were the same. They ask for home tuition in the same subject, the same year and the same area, which is what they asked for last time, and leave out the only information that would actually help: what the previous tutor covered, what she tried that did not work, and why the arrangement ended. Parents searching for the best IGCSE tutors in Mumbai after one has already failed are not starting from zero. They are starting from minus one month, because the new tutor will spend that month rediscovering what the old one already knew.

1. Tell us what ended the last arrangement, honestly: the tutor moved out of Mumbai, your child changed schools, the slot stopped working, or the two of them simply did not get on. 2. Send whatever written record exists, even if it is three WhatsApp messages and a photograph of a marked paper. 3. We identify what the replacement must have that the last one lacked, which is often the opposite quality rather than more of the same. 4. We propose two or three tutors who teach that specification and already travel in your zone, with the handover material attached so the first session starts where the last one stopped.

The honest reason this step is skipped so often is that it feels like admitting something. A parent who has already changed an IGCSE tutor Mumbai once is reluctant to say the first one was wrong, and especially reluctant to say the student would not do the work. Neither of those is embarrassing and both are useful. A tutor who knows the student stopped attempting homework after October will plan the first fortnight completely differently from one who thinks she is dealing with a knowledge gap.

We do not rank the people on the shortlist, and we will not tell you that one of them is the strongest tutor available in the city. What we will tell you is which one has taught this specification most recently, which one has handled a mid-course takeover before, and which one is likely to clash with your child in the same way the last one did. The third of those is the one worth reading twice.

sections.heading: The two-year IGCSE course almost nobody finishes with one tutor
paragraphs: The International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) runs across Years 9 to 11 in most Mumbai schools, which is two to three calendar years of weekly sessions. Very little in this city stays fixed for that long. Home tutors finish postgraduate courses and leave for full-time teaching. They move from Chembur to Pune, or from Vikhroli to Bengaluru. Families relocate between Thane and the Western Suburbs for work. Students switch schools and sometimes switch boards. And occasionally the arrangement simply outgrows itself, because the tutor who was right for a nervous Year 9 is not right for a Year 11 eight weeks from a board exam.

That last case is the one families fight hardest and should fight least. Year 9 teaching is confidence work: slow, patient, forgiving, aimed at a thirteen-year-old who is still deciding what kind of student she is. Year 11 teaching is exam engineering: timed papers, mark schemes, command words, the discipline of abandoning a question that is costing too much time. A tutor who is excellent at the first is not automatically poor at the second, but they are different jobs, and pretending otherwise out of loyalty costs a student the most valuable term she has.

The board structure makes continuity matter more than it would elsewhere. Cambridge International Education splits many subjects into Core and Extended tiers with different papers and different grade ceilings, while Pearson Edexcel more often runs one tier with the harder content at the end of the paper. A tier decision made in Year 10 constrains everything afterwards, and a new tutor who does not know which tier was chosen, or why, will spend weeks teaching at the wrong level. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 a tutor Mumbai families bring in halfway through needs the tier in writing on day one.

At International Baccalaureate (IB) schools there is a further thread to keep intact. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) feeds into IGCSE at some schools and runs alongside it at others, and the subject and tier choices made here decide which Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) options stay open in the Diploma Programme (DP). A student who quietly drops to Core Maths in Year 10 has made a DP decision without anyone recording it as one. The handover note is where that gets written down.

sections.heading: Which subject records matter most when a tutor changes?
paragraphs: Four records matter and the rest are optional. The running error log, meaning the list of mistakes this student makes repeatedly rather than the topics she has covered. The marked scripts with the teacher's comments intact. A note of what was tried and did not work. And the board, tier and subject option sheet. Hand a new tutor those four and the first session is teaching. Hand over nothing and the first month is archaeology.

The error log is the one families never have and always need. A topic list tells a new tutor where the class has reached, which the school timetable would have told her anyway. An error log tells her that this student consistently drops the units in Physics calculations, loses the negative sign when rearranging, and writes conclusions in Chemistry that do not reference the data. Those patterns took the previous tutor two months to see. Rediscovering them costs the new one the same two months, and in Year 11 there is no second two months available.

Subject by subject the handover weight differs. Mathematics transfers most cleanly because the error patterns are concrete and visible in the working. Sciences transfer reasonably well if practical and coursework components are documented, since a replacement needs to know what has been submitted and what is outstanding. English Literature transfers worst of all, because the set texts, the essays already written and the particular argument a student has been building are hard to reconstruct from marks alone. If you are changing an English tutor, send the essays, not the grades.

Choice decisions need their own line in the record. Whether the sciences were taken separately or as Combined Science, whether Additional Mathematics was added, which tier was chosen and on whose advice, and what internal or coursework component each subject carries. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents bring in at short notice will otherwise form her own view in week two and start gently relitigating decisions the family already made, which wastes everybody's time and unsettles the student.

sections.heading: Why tutors leave: the six Mumbai markets and how families move between them
paragraphs: The Central Suburbs produce more handovers than anywhere else in Mumbai, Maharashtra, and the reason is structural rather than cultural. Powai, Chandivali, Kanjurmarg, Vikhroli, Ghatkopar and Mulund hold a large international school population with a transient working parent base, so families arrive for a three-year posting and leave mid-course. Powai compounds it by having no station of its own: every tutor arrives by road along the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road or the Eastern Express Highway from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and a tutor who changes jobs to an office on the other side of that road will usually give up the slot rather than the job.

The Eastern Suburbs behave similarly for a different reason. Chembur, Govandi, Bhandup, Mulund and Wadala are well served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway, the Eastern Freeway and the Chembur to Wadala monorail, and that connectivity cuts both ways: a tutor based in Chembur can take work in Fort or Lower Parel once the Eastern Freeway makes it viable, and your weekday evening slot is what gets dropped. The Santacruz Chembur Link Road has the same effect westward. Good connectivity creates options for a home tutor, and options create turnover.

In the Western Suburbs the churn is about distance rather than opportunity. Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri, Oshiwara, Goregaon, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar sit along the Western Line, the Western Express Highway and Link Road, with Metro Line 1 crossing at Andheri and Metro Lines 2A and 7 covering the Dahisar to Gundavali run. Arrangements that match along the line hold. Those that cross it lapse quietly around the second monsoon. South Mumbai, by contrast, has low churn and a small pool: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road, Tardeo and Worli are short distances apart but slow in the evening peak, and the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 have improved the approach without changing the arithmetic much. When a tutor is lost here, the replacement usually comes from the same few kilometres.

Navi Mumbai and Thane generate a third kind of handover: the family that moves. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are connected by Palm Beach Road, the Sion Panvel Highway, the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and the Belapur to Pendhar metro, and the Atal Setu has pulled the island city closer. In Thane, the station area, Pokhran Road, Majiwada and the Ghodbunder Road corridor out to Kasarvadavali form one market where travel time, not distance, decides everything. Families relocating from Thane to Powai or from Nerul to Chembur almost always lose the tutor in the move, which is exactly the moment the written record earns its keep.

sections.heading: Changing schools mid-IGCSE and what it does to the tutoring
paragraphs: A school change between Year 9 and Year 11 is more disruptive than a tutor change and the two often arrive together. The Mumbai academic year opens in June, mocks fall across December and January, coursework deadlines cluster in January and February, and the examined series runs in May and June. A student moving in October has missed the first assessment cycle at the new school and arrives in the middle of topic sequences that were taught in a different order. Schools cover the same specification in different sequences, so a transfer can leave a genuine hole in the middle of a subject that nobody notices until the mock.

The move sometimes changes the board as well. A student leaving Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East for a Pearson Edexcel school, or moving from Oberoi International School near the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road to an IGCSE pathway at JBCN International School in Chembur, is not simply changing buildings. Families at NES International School in Mulund West, Podar International School in Powai, Witty International School, Ryan Global School, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, Gopi Birla Memorial School in Walkeshwar and Singapore International School in Dahisar East all run to their own internal deadlines, and the new school's mock week is the date a replacement tutor should be planning backwards from.

IB Gram is an independent platform. We are not affiliated with any school named on this page, nor with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and we have no visibility of any school's internal marks, predicted grades or paper setting. Naming a school here tells you only where families in that pocket of the city send their children and what calendar they live by. A tutor who claims to know what a particular school will put on its mock is making something up.

The practical rule for timing a handover is to avoid doing it in the dark. Changing tutors in June or July, when the new academic year has just opened, costs least: the re-diagnosis month lands in a period with no deadlines in it. Changing in late September or October is survivable. Changing in January, a fortnight before coursework is due, means the new tutor spends the only available time learning the student instead of teaching her. If the current arrangement is failing in January, change anyway, but go in expecting triage rather than a fresh start.

sections.heading: Can home tuition survive a move across Mumbai, or should you switch online?
paragraphs: If you move more than one zone, assume the home tuition arrangement ends and plan the handover rather than hoping. A home tutor who has been coming to your flat in Vikhroli every Tuesday will not start driving to Kandivali, and asking her to try produces two months of late arrivals and a resentful ending. The better move is to decide at the point of relocation: either a new IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai on the other side, briefed properly with the old tutor's notes, or the same tutor continuing online with the relationship intact.

Keeping the existing tutor online is genuinely the stronger option in one specific case, which is a Year 11 in the last two terms. At that point the relationship and the accumulated knowledge of this student's error patterns are worth more than physical presence, and the re-diagnosis month you avoid is a month you do not have. An IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai who already knows that your daughter drops units and rushes the last question will outperform a better teacher who is meeting her in February. Earlier in the course, the arithmetic reverses: a Year 9 is better served by a new person in the room than a familiar face on a screen.

Hybrid is the quiet answer to the handover problem itself. Where the outgoing tutor is willing, we ask for two overlapping sessions: one where both tutors are present, usually with the outgoing one online and the new one at the dining table, and one where the new tutor teaches and the old one has already left. It is not always possible, because tutors leave for reasons that make goodwill scarce. When it is possible it removes most of the lost month, and it is the single most useful thing a family can arrange.

The travel arithmetic deserves one blunt line, because it is what breaks most arrangements before anyone admits it. A tutor spending ninety minutes on the road for a sixty minute session is in an arrangement with an expiry date, and the expiry usually falls in the second monsoon rather than at a natural break. If the only candidates with real depth in your subject live across the city, choose online deliberately at the start instead of arranging a handover you will have to run again in eight months.

sections.heading: What we verify about a replacement tutor in Mumbai, and what the outgoing tutor owes you
paragraphs: Every tutor gives us government photograph identification, named qualifications with the awarding institution, and a teaching history we can question. For a mid-course replacement we check two further things. First, whether the tutor has taught this exact specification recently enough to know what changed, because a replacement joining in Year 11 has no time to discover a syllabus revision the hard way. Second, whether she has taken over from another tutor before, which is a distinct skill: it requires reading someone else's notes without contradicting them in front of the student.

The outgoing tutor owes you something too, and most will give it if asked before the relationship sours. A list of topics covered with dates. The error log, or whatever version of it exists. An honest sentence about what did not work, which is the most valuable item and the one most likely to go unsaid. And the return of anything belonging to the student: marked scripts, annotated past papers, the notebook. Ask for all of it in the same message in which you end the arrangement, not a week later.

Four questions are worth putting to any IGCSE private tutor Mumbai proposes as a replacement. Ask what she would do in the first session given the handover notes, and listen for whether she has read them. Ask what she would keep from the previous tutor's approach, because an answer of nothing is a warning. Ask what she will want from the student between sessions. And ask how she will tell you if the student is not doing it, which is the question that separates a professional from someone who will let a term drift politely.

The documentation point is worth stating plainly because it is the one structural fix available to families. Keep the record in your house. The error log, the marked scripts, the topic list and the handover notes belong to your child, not to whoever is teaching her this term. Whether you find tutors through us, through a neighbour, or by typing IGCSE tutors near me into a Mumbai search box, insist on this from the first session. It costs nothing while things are going well, and it is the difference between a handover and a restart.

sections.heading: How to run a handover instead of a cold restart
paragraphs: The month after a tutor change is the most wasted month in IGCSE tutoring, and it is wasted the same way every time. The new tutor arrives, is told the subject and the year group, and spends four sessions doing what any competent professional would do with no information: diagnosing. She sets a past paper. She watches the working. She finds the foundation gap. All of this is good practice and all of it duplicates work the previous tutor completed in October. Families comparing the best IGCSE tutors in Mumbai tend to assume a better tutor would diagnose faster. She will not, because the limit is information, not ability.

A handover has four parts and takes about twenty minutes of somebody's time. One: the artefact bundle, meaning the error log, the marked scripts, the topic list with dates and the tier and board written down. Two: the failure note, a few sentences on what was tried and did not work, which prevents the new tutor from repeating a failed approach for three weeks before concluding the same thing. Three: the human note, covering how this student responds to pressure, what time of evening she is useless, and what she will not say out loud. Four: a conversation between the two tutors, if goodwill permits, lasting one phone call.

Families resist the third part because it feels disloyal to describe your own child candidly to a stranger. It is the part that saves the most time. A tutor who is told in advance that this student goes silent rather than admitting confusion will check differently from session one, instead of spending a month mistaking silence for understanding. A tutor who is told the student is sharp but refuses to write anything down will not waste the first fortnight on content she already knows. None of this is in a report card and none of it is recoverable by observation in under a month.

Sometimes the right answer is to break the chain deliberately, and a handover should not be confused with continuity for its own sake. If the previous arrangement failed because the tutor taught at the wrong level, the new one needs the records but not the approach. If it failed because of personality, the handover note should say so in neutral language and the new tutor should be chosen for the opposite temperament. And if a student has rebuilt a story about herself in which she cannot do the subject, a fresh start genuinely helps. The judgement is whether what is being carried forward is knowledge, which is always worth keeping, or a pattern, which usually is not. The practical test: would the previous tutor's notes change what the new one does next Tuesday? If yes, hand them over. If the honest answer is that nothing in them is actionable, you did not have a record worth transferring and the real lesson is to start keeping one now, for the tutor after this one.
bullets: The lost month after a change is an information problem, not a talent problem

sections.heading: What does the first month with a new tutor actually look like?
paragraphs: With a proper handover, the first session is teaching and the first month produces visible behaviour change: working written out without prompting, questions brought to the session, a shorter lag between school teaching and comprehension. Without a handover, the first month is diagnosis and you should expect nothing measurable from it. Knowing which of those two months you bought is the point. Judging a new tutor harshly at week four for doing necessary archaeology is how families end up on their fourth tutor.

By the end of one term the comparison that matters is against the previous arrangement, not against an ideal. Is the student doing more unprompted work than she was? Has the pattern of lost marks changed shape, or only in size? Can the new tutor describe your daughter's specific failure modes without looking at notes? That last question is the most reliable single test of whether a term was used well, and it works even when marks have not yet moved, which at this stage they frequently have not.

Over a full exam cycle, the honest expectation after a mid-course change is that you will recover the lost ground and then gain, rather than gain from where the last tutor left off. That is not pessimism, it is arithmetic: a handover month is a month. Mathematics recovers fastest because the error patterns are visible in the working and can be re-found quickly. English Literature recovers slowest, since a new tutor inherits essays built on an argument she did not help construct. We do not guarantee grades, and a platform that offers to after a disrupted year is not being straight with you.

Two warnings about serial changes. First, every change resets the clock, so a family on its third tutor in Year 11 has spent three months on diagnosis and roughly none on momentum. Second, repeated changes teach a student that the arrangement is temporary, and a sixteen-year-old who expects this tutor to be gone by March invests accordingly. If you are considering a second change inside one academic year, the conversation worth having first is whether the problem is actually the tutor, the tier, the timetable or the amount of work being done between sessions.

sections.heading: Setting up IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai that outlives one tutor
paragraphs: Start the record on day one of the next home tuition arrangement rather than at the end of it. Ask the incoming tutor for three things in writing after the first six weeks: the list of repeated errors she is seeing, the topics covered with dates, and anything she has tried that did not work. Keep them in one place in your house. It takes a tutor ten minutes a term and it means the next handover, whenever it comes, costs you a week instead of a month.

For the match itself, send us the area, the subject and tier, the year group, the two evenings that genuinely work, and whatever exists of the previous arrangement's history. We come back with two or three tutors who teach that specification and already travel in your part of the city, with notes on what each would do differently from the last one. Where the outgoing tutor is willing, we will try to arrange an overlapping session so the student watches the handover happen rather than being handed to a stranger.

The first session with the replacement is deliberately not a fresh diagnostic if the records exist. It is a check: the tutor confirms the three or four error patterns in the notes are still live, finds anything the previous tutor missed, and sets the first six weeks against the next real deadline on the school calendar. You get that plan in writing afterwards. It stays with your family, and the tutor after this one will start from it.

faqs.question: What does searching for the best IGCSE tutors in Mumbai get me that I do not already have?
faqs.answer: Mostly it gets you a shortlist, which is only half the problem if you have had a tutor before. The part that changes outcomes on a second or third match is the handover: giving the incoming tutor the error log, the marked scripts, the tier and the honest account of what failed last time. A capable tutor with that information outperforms a stronger one without it for at least the first two months. We ask for it at the briefing stage because families almost never volunteer it unprompted.

faqs.question: Our tutor is leaving Mumbai in two months. What should we ask her for before she goes?
faqs.answer: Ask now, while the relationship is still good, because goodwill evaporates in the final fortnight. Request four things: a dated list of topics covered, the running log of repeated errors she has noticed, a few honest sentences on what she tried that did not work, and the return of all marked scripts and annotated papers. Then ask whether she would take one phone call from the replacement. Most tutors say yes if asked early and politely, and that call is worth more than everything else combined.

faqs.question: Can a new tutor come to our building in Kharghar on a weekday evening, or is online safer?
faqs.answer: Both work in Navi Mumbai, and the deciding factor is which year your child is in. Kharghar, Belapur, Nerul, Vashi and Panvel have a local tutor pool connected by Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway, and node to node travel holds up across a full year, so a Year 9 or Year 10 is well served by home classes. For a Year 11 in the final two terms, keeping an existing tutor online usually beats starting fresh with someone local, because the handover month is time you no longer have.

faqs.question: Will IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai change when we switch tutors?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the reasons are worth understanding before you negotiate. Rates move with board and tier, since Extended and Additional Mathematics cost more than Core. They move with subject scarcity, which is why a replacement Computer Science or Additional Mathematics tutor can cost more than the person who left. They move with travel distance, session length and frequency, and with whether the format is at home, online or hybrid. A mid-year replacement in a scarce subject is the most expensive combination, which is an argument for not leaving the change until February.

faqs.question: Our society requires fresh approval for a new visitor. How do we handle the changeover?
faqs.answer: Register the new tutor before the last session with the old one, so there is no gap. We send the replacement's name, photograph identification and the fixed weekly slot in advance, which is what most Mumbai complexes need to issue a standing entry rather than a visitor pass each week. If your building uses a resident approval app, note that at the matching stage, because it means somebody has to be home at the start of every session and that narrows which evening slots are realistic for both tutors during the overlap.

faqs.question: My daughter liked her old tutor and is upset about the change. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal and it is worth managing rather than overriding. Tell her the change is happening and why, in plain terms, before the new tutor is introduced, and let her be present when the handover notes are passed on. Students who watch the handover treat the new tutor as a continuation; students who are simply presented with a stranger treat the first month as a negotiation. Where the outgoing tutor is willing to join one overlapping session, even online, the difference in how quickly a sixteen-year-old settles is noticeable.

faqs.question: We are moving from Thane to the Western Suburbs. Can we keep the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not in person, and trying usually ends badly. A tutor used to a Pokhran Road or Ghodbunder Road run will not commit to Andheri or Malad for a weekly evening slot, and the arrangement dissolves over two months of late arrivals rather than ending cleanly. Decide at the point of the move: either continue with that tutor online, which preserves everything she knows about your child, or arrange a properly briefed replacement in the new area. The one option to avoid is leaving it undecided and discovering the answer in November.

faqs.question: How many tutors is too many across the IGCSE years?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed number, but each change costs roughly a month, so three changes inside Year 11 means three months of diagnosis and very little momentum. More importantly, repeated changes teach a student that tutoring is temporary, and she will invest accordingly. If you are considering a second change within one academic year, examine whether the recurring problem is the tutor at all. Wrong tier, an impossible slot, sessions being cancelled more often than reported, and homework simply not being done all masquerade as tutor problems.

faqs.question: The new tutor wants to redo the diagnostic even though we sent notes. Is that a bad sign?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but ask her why. A short verification, meaning one past paper section to confirm the recorded error patterns are still live, is good practice and takes part of one session. A full four-week rediagnosis when a detailed record exists means either she has not read the notes or she does not trust them, and both are worth saying out loud in week one. The useful question is what specifically she thinks the previous tutor got wrong, since a clear answer is reassuring and a vague one is not.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring make handovers easier than home classes?
faqs.answer: Marginally, and in one specific way: online sessions tend to leave a written trail of shared documents and annotated screens that a replacement can actually read. Home sessions generate better teaching and worse records, because the work ends up in a notebook that leaves with the tutor. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes Mumbai families run, the fix is simple rather than technological: photograph the week's working before the tutor leaves, and keep it. The record problem is a habit problem, not a format problem.

faqs.question: Should we change the tutor or change the tier if progress has stalled?
faqs.answer: Check the tier first, because it is cheaper to fix and more often the cause. A student placed on Extended when the evidence says Core will stall regardless of who teaches her, and three tutor changes will not move her. Ask the current tutor to mark one full past paper at each tier and look at the difference. If Core produces a solid performance and Extended produces a scattered one, the tier is the problem. If both look similar, the issue is engagement or teaching, and then a change of tutor is the conversation to have.

faqs.question: Do you publish rankings so we can just hire the strongest tutor available?
faqs.answer: No. A ranking needs one scale, and the qualities that make someone right for a mid-course takeover in Year 11 are different from what a nervous Year 9 needs, so any single list would mislead somebody. What we provide is two or three candidates with written reasoning, including what each is weaker at and how each has handled taking over from another tutor. Searching for the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is a reasonable thing to type into Google, but the useful answer is a match with a handover attached. IB Gram is independent and does not guarantee grades.

A tutor who already teaches a Diploma Programme (DP) student at Mulund West on Tuesdays and Thursdays can hold a standing slot in Bhandup on the same two evenings for two full years. A tutor with no other family on this stretch of the Central Line usually takes the booking, teaches well for six weeks, and then starts asking to shift the time. sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP or IGCSE: which structure is your child actually in?
paragraphs: Four structures cover almost every international-board family here. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP) up to Year 5, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) across Years 6 to 10, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in Years 11 and 12. IGCSE, offered under Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, sits in Years 9 to 11 and ends in a terminal exam series. Parents often say their child is doing IB when the school actually runs MYP for three years and IGCSE for two.

That distinction changes what a tutor has to do on day one. MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria, usually labelled A to D, each with its own strands and achievement-level descriptors, and the task instructions carry command terms that decide how much credit an answer can earn. A student who writes a good answer to the wrong command term loses marks a tutor can recover in a fortnight. There is no percentage to chase, so a tutor who teaches MYP as if it were a scored test will miss the criterion the teacher is actually marking.

The DP is a different load again: six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), with an Internal Assessment (IA) in nearly every one of them, plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the creativity, activity, service requirement running alongside. The exam papers matter, but the IAs are where most families lose ground, because they are coursework with soft internal deadlines that slide until they collide.

IGCSE is tiered. Many subjects offer a Core and an Extended route with different papers and different grade ceilings, and the school decides entries during Year 10. The move from MYP criteria to an IGCSE mark scheme is the sharpest change most students here feel, and it usually arrives in the same term as the first serious set of past papers. A family in Bhandup with one child in MYP and one sitting IGCSE needs two different teaching styles, not one tutor doing the same lesson twice.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: the decisions a Bhandup family makes
paragraphs: Three decisions do most of the damage or most of the good: which subjects a child carries forward, whether each one is taken at HL or SL in the DP, and whether an IGCSE subject is entered for Core or Extended. All three are usually settled months before anyone thinks of calling a tutor, and all three are reversible for a short window and then not. A tutor is far more useful in the term before the choice than in the term after it.

A worked example from the Cambridge side. A Year 10 student at Hiranandani Foundation School taking Chemistry 0620 and heading for Extended will sit Paper 2 rather than Paper 1, and Paper 4 rather than Paper 3, which means the theory paper expects mole calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction pathways that the Core paper never asks for. Alongside that comes either Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, and those two reward completely different preparation. Paper 6 is a reading-and-inference paper about experiments; it rewards practice with tables, anomalous results and sources of error, not more bench time. A tutor who does not know which of the two the school has entered is guessing at half the course.

On the IB side the arithmetic is the IA count. A DP student carries an internal assessment in most of their six subjects, and the school spreads the deadlines across DP1 and DP2 with the best intentions. In practice the drafts bunch, because teachers set drafts before their own reporting dates. A DP2 student in Bhandup can find a Chemistry IA draft, an Economics commentary and the EE first full draft all landing inside three weeks of each other in the second term, with mocks the month after.

Which is why subject breadth in a tutor matters less than honesty about range. Nobody is a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai, whatever a listing claims. One good teacher can usually hold two related subjects, coach the structure of an IA in a third, and should say plainly when a fourth needs a specialist. We would rather put a second person in your flat on a different evening than let one tutor bluff through an HL Physics paper they last looked at in college.

sections.heading: Kanjurmarg, Mulund West and Powai: the route your Bhandup home tutor is already on
paragraphs: One tutor working in Bhandup will normally also cover Kanjurmarg, Mulund West and Powai, because those four places sit on a single workable evening route. Bhandup station is on the Central Line between Kurla and Mulund, and LBS Marg runs parallel to the tracks on the west side, which is how most tutors actually arrive: train to Bhandup, then an auto along LBS Marg, or a two-wheeler the whole way from Powai.

Each neighbour reaches Bhandup differently and that shapes the clock. Mulund West is one stop up, so a tutor finishing there at 7.30pm can be at your door by about 8. Kanjurmarg is one stop down and just as quick. Powai is the odd one out in this part of Mumbai, Maharashtra: it is physically central but has no station of its own, so tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, usually down JVLR. A Powai-based tutor therefore comes to Bhandup by car or bike along JVLR and LBS Marg, and their arrival time is set by whatever they were doing in Powai first. For tutors living further west, Metro Line 1 from Andheri to Ghatkopar plus one short hop is more reliable than the Eastern Express Highway at 6pm, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road only helps outside the peak.

Inside Bhandup the last kilometre decides punctuality more than the first ten. A family in Runwal Greens off LBS Marg is an easy auto from the station in dry weather and a twenty-minute problem in heavy monsoon rain. Ashford Royale sits towards the Mulund end, which suits a tutor coming down from NES International School but adds minutes for anyone arriving from Kanjurmarg. Tell us your tower and your gate rule at the start and the slot we propose will be one the tutor can actually keep in July.

This is also why IB and IGCSE home tuition in Bhandup holds together better than the same request in a pocket with no neighbouring demand. Parents search for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Bhandup and assume near means the tutor's home address. The useful definition of near is the tutor's Tuesday route. An IB and IGCSE private tutor in Bhandup whose other family is two stops away will be here every week; one travelling from Borivali will not, however good their first session was.
